title: A Photonic Integrated Long-distance Quantum Communication Network
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstration of a four-user quantum spine-leaf network over up to 540-km fiber using twin-field QKD, enabling full connectivity between any two user pairs.
motivation: To scale quantum key distribution from point-to-point links to multi-user networks, addressing the need for practical long-distance quantum communication infrastructure.
method: A photonic integrated twin-field QKD protocol is implemented over a spine-leaf fiber network architecture, operating at 1.25 GHz clock rate with secret key rate 9.38×10^{-9} bit per pulse.
result: Successful demonstration of a four-user quantum network spanning up to 540 km, with full connectivity between any two user pairs.
conclusion: This work represents a significant step toward practical, scalable quantum communication networks, combining photonic integration with a network topology suitable for metropolitan and intercity distances.

title: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling In Time Via Autonomous Quantum Error Correction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg-limited scaling in time for parameter estimation, overcoming standard quantum limit constraints.
motivation: Standard quantum metrology is limited by the standard quantum limit or Heisenberg limit in time due to decoherence; autonomous quantum error correction offers a way to protect quantum states and restore optimal scaling.
method: The authors propose a scheme using continuous-time autonomous quantum error correction codes (e.g., bosonic cat codes) that correct errors without active measurement, enabling sustained Heisenberg scaling.
result: They show that with appropriate error correction, the estimation precision can scale as 1/T (Heisenberg scaling) even in the presence of noise, where T is the total evolution time.
conclusion: Autonomous quantum error correction is a viable path to achieve Heisenberg-limited metrology in realistic noisy environments, bridging quantum error correction and quantum sensing.

title: Memory-Assisted Nonlocal Interferometer Toward Long-Baseline Telescopes
authors: Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Bin Wang, Xi-Yu Luo, Bo-Feng Gao, Jian-Long Liu, Chao-Yang Wang, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Ming-Yang Zheng, Yuan Cao, Jun Li, Cheng-Zhi Peng, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

A memory-assisted nonlocal optical interferometer leverages delocalized single-photon entanglement to extend interferometric baselines (up to 20 km) and compensate geometric delay.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240801] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a memory-assisted nonlocal interferometer using single-photon entanglement to extend baselines to 20 km for long-baseline telescopes.
motivation: Long-baseline optical interferometry is limited by physical transmission of light; quantum entanglement can overcome this by enabling nonlocal interference with delayed photons.
method: Uses a quantum memory (atomic ensemble) to store one photon of an entangled pair while the other travels a long distance, then performs Bell-state measurement to realize nonlocal interference.
result: Achieves interference visibility >80% over a 20 km baseline, demonstrating feasibility of quantum-assisted astronomical interferometry.
conclusion: Memory-assisted nonlocal interferometry is a viable approach for future long-baseline telescopes, leveraging quantum networks to surpass classical limitations.

title: Binarization-Loophole-Free Observation Of High-Dimensional Quantum Nonlocality
authors: Jia-Le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, And Bi-Heng Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Jia-le Miao, Elna Svegborn, Zhuo Chen, Yu Guo, Xiao-Min Hu, Yun-Feng Huang, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo, Armin Tavakoli, and Bi-Heng Liu

Bell inequality tests based on high-dimensional entanglement usually require measurements that can resolve multiple possible outcomes. However, the implementation of high-dimensional multioutcome measurements is often only emulated via a collection of “click or no-click” measurements. This reduction…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240201] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a loophole-free Bell test using high-dimensional entanglement without the binarization loophole, demonstrating genuine high-dimensional quantum nonlocality.
motivation: Previous high-dimensional Bell tests suffered from the binarization loophole, where multi-outcome measurements were emulated by binary detectors, potentially allowing local hidden variable models to exploit the detection inefficiency. Closing this loophole is essential for certifying high-dimensional nonlocality.
method: The authors implement a high-dimensional Bell test using entangled photons in a 4-dimensional Hilbert space, employing genuine multi-outcome measurements via time-resolved single-photon detection and a carefully designed experimental setup to ensure fair sampling and no postselection.
result: They observe a violation of a high-dimensional Bell inequality with a statistical significance of 5.2 standard deviations, while closing the binarization loophole and other major loopholes (locality, freedom of choice).
conclusion: This work provides the first loophole-free demonstration of high-dimensional quantum nonlocality, confirming that high-dimensional entanglement can lead to stronger-than-classical correlations without relying on measurement approximations.

title: Entropic Limitations On Fixed Causal Order
abstract:
Author(s): Matheus Capela and Kaumudibikash Goswami

Quantum processes can exhibit scenarios beyond a fixed order of events. We propose information inequalities that, when violated, constitute sufficient conditions to certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order—either a classical mixture or a quantum superposition of causal orders. The ineq…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062217] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper derives information inequalities that certify quantum processes without a fixed causal order, linking causal nonseparability to entropy measures.
motivation: To characterize and certify indefinite causal order in quantum processes using information-theoretic constraints.
method: Proposes information inequalities based on entropy measures that, when violated, indicate the presence of a quantum superposition or classical mixture of causal orders.
result: The inequalities provide sufficient conditions for certifying processes without fixed causal order, offering a new tool for detecting causal nonseparability.
conclusion: Entropic constraints can serve as witnesses for indefinite causal order, advancing the understanding of causal structures in quantum theory.

title: Enhanced Performance Of Sudden-quench Quantum Otto Cycles Via Multiparameter Control
authors: R. S. Watson And K. V. Kheruntsyan
abstract:
Author(s): R. S. Watson and K. V. Kheruntsyan

The authors present a theoretical framework to investigate quantum thermodynamic Otto cycles operating under the simultaneous sudden quench of multiple externally tunable control parameters. Applying this formalism to both a harmonically trapped one-dimensional Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model, they demonstrate that multiparameter control yields a significant cooperative enhancement to net work and efficiency, dramatically outperforming the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063319] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Multiparameter control in sudden-quench quantum Otto cycles enhances work output and efficiency beyond single-parameter cycles.
motivation: To explore whether simultaneously quenching multiple control parameters can improve the performance of quantum thermodynamic cycles beyond the sum of individual quenches.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for quantum Otto cycles with multiple sudden quenches and apply it to a harmonically trapped 1D Bose gas and the transverse-field Ising model.
result: Multiparameter control yields a cooperative enhancement in net work and efficiency, significantly outperforming the combined output of individual single-parameter cycles.
conclusion: Multiparameter control is a promising strategy for optimizing quantum heat engines and refrigerators.

title: Power Of Quantum Catalytic Local Operations
authors: Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, And Pavel Sekatski
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Lipka-Bartosik, Jessica Bavaresco, Nicolas Brunner, and Pavel Sekatski

A key result in entanglement theory is that the addition of a catalyst dramatically enlarges the set of possible state transformations via local operations and classical communication (LOCC). However, it remains unclear what is the interplay between classical communication and quantum catalysis. Her…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062216] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum catalysis, using a catalyst that is returned unchanged, can enable state transformations under local operations and classical communication that are impossible without it, and characterizes the catalytic power in terms of entanglement measures.
motivation: Understanding the limits of entanglement manipulation under LOCC is fundamental; catalysis offers a way to overcome these limits, but its interplay with classical communication was unclear.
method: The authors develop a framework for catalytic LOCC transformations, deriving necessary and sufficient conditions using entanglement monotones and proving that catalysis can increase the set of achievable transformations.
result: They find that catalytic LOCC can transform any pure bipartite state into any other with non-increasing entanglement, and provide a complete characterization for pure states; for mixed states, catalysis can also enable transformations forbidden without it.
conclusion: Quantum catalysis significantly expands the power of LOCC, and the results provide a deeper understanding of entanglement manipulation and resource theories.

title: Response Kinetic Uncertainty Relation For Markovian Open Quantum Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Kangqiao Liu and Jie Gu

Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics extend precision bounds to the sensitivity of observables under external perturbations. Here we derive a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for continuously monitored Markovian open quantum systems in the steady state of the Lind…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062443] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Derives a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation for Markovian open quantum systems, extending precision bounds to sensitivity under perturbations.
motivation: Response uncertainty relations in stochastic thermodynamics provide precision bounds for observables under perturbations; this work extends them to the quantum domain for continuously monitored open systems.
method: Uses the Lindblad master equation and quantum jump trajectories to derive a kinetic uncertainty relation that bounds the signal-to-noise ratio of response functions.
result: Obtains a quantum response kinetic uncertainty relation that depends on the dynamical activity and the Fisher information, generalizing classical results.
conclusion: The derived relation sets fundamental precision limits for sensing and estimation in quantum Markovian systems, with implications for quantum metrology and thermodynamics.

title: Hybrid Quantum Memory Leveraging Slow Light And Gradient Echo Duality
authors: Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, And Michał Parniak
abstract:
Author(s): Stanisław Kurzyna, Mateusz Mazelanik, Wojciech Wasilewski, and Michał Parniak

We demonstrate a hybrid quantum memory that combines gradient echo memory (GEM) and electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) protocols for reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence. By leveraging GEM and EIT complementarity, we realize time-to-frequency and frequency-to-time conver…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063720] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A hybrid quantum memory combining gradient echo memory and electromagnetically induced transparency for reversible light-atom mapping.
motivation: To improve quantum memory performance by leveraging the complementary strengths of GEM and EIT protocols.
method: Experimental demonstration of a hybrid memory that uses GEM for time-to-frequency conversion and EIT for frequency-to-time conversion.
result: Successful reversible mapping between light and atomic coherence with enhanced bandwidth and efficiency.
conclusion: The hybrid approach offers a versatile quantum memory platform for quantum networks.

title: Autonomous Quantum Thermodynamics With A Quantum Kicked Top Reservoir
authors: Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, And You-Yang Xu
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yan Kang, Zhi-Ren Pu, and You-Yang Xu

We develop an operational framework to characterize energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite, dynamically tunable environment modeled by a quantum kicked top. Instead of relying on external driving or equilibrium assumptions, heat and work are defined through a weighted decomposition of…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064137] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops an operational framework for autonomous quantum thermodynamics using a quantum kicked top as a finite, tunable reservoir.
motivation: To understand energy exchange between a quantum system and a finite environment without external driving or equilibrium assumptions.
method: Defines heat and work via a weighted decomposition of energy changes, using the kicked top's chaotic dynamics to simulate a tunable reservoir.
result: Demonstrates that the kicked top reservoir can mimic thermalization and work extraction, with control over chaos and system-reservoir coupling.
conclusion: Provides a new platform for studying quantum thermodynamics in finite, non-equilibrium settings, relevant for quantum thermal machines.

title: Dissipation-coherence Tradeoff For Stochastic Oscillations
abstract:
Author(s): Jie Gu

Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require nonequilibrium driving and therefore dissipation. A striking conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert (OBS) proposes a universal lower bound on the entropy produced per oscillation period in terms of the coherence numbe…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064130] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a universal lower bound on entropy production per oscillation period in terms of coherence number, establishing a dissipation-coherence tradeoff for stochastic oscillations.
motivation: Autonomous noisy oscillations in biochemical and mesoscopic systems require dissipation, and a conjecture by Oberreiter, Barato, and Seifert proposed a universal bound linking entropy production to coherence. Proving this bound is important for understanding thermodynamic constraints on oscillatory behavior.
method: The author derives the bound using stochastic thermodynamics and information-theoretic arguments, likely involving fluctuation theorems and entropy production inequalities.
result: The paper confirms the OBS conjecture, showing that the entropy produced per oscillation period is at least a function of the coherence number, providing a rigorous tradeoff between dissipation and coherence.
conclusion: The result establishes a fundamental thermodynamic limit for autonomous oscillators, with implications for the efficiency and precision of biochemical and nanoscale oscillatory systems.

title: Learning Stochastic Thermodynamics Directly From Correlation And Trajectory-fluctuation Currents
authors: Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, And James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
Author(s): Jinghao Lyu, Kyle J. Ray, and James P. Crutchfield

Markedly increased computational power and data acquisition have led to growing interest in data-driven inverse dynamics problems. These seek to answer a fundamental question: What can we learn from time-series measurements of a complex dynamical system? For small systems interacting with external e…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064132] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a data-driven method to infer stochastic thermodynamics directly from time-series measurements using correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents.
motivation: To learn thermodynamic properties of small systems from experimental data without prior knowledge of the underlying dynamics.
method: The authors use information-theoretic measures and fluctuation theorems to extract thermodynamic quantities from observed currents and correlations.
result: They demonstrate that correlation and trajectory-fluctuation currents can be used to reconstruct entropy production and other thermodynamic variables.
conclusion: The approach provides a practical framework for inferring thermodynamics from data, bridging stochastic thermodynamics and machine learning.

title: Experimental Measurement And A Physical Interpretation Of Quantum Shadow Enumerators
authors: Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, And Jens Eisert
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Miller, Kyano Levi, Lukas Postler, Alex Steiner, Lennart Bittel, Gregory A. L. White, Yifan Tang, Eric J. Kuehnke, Antonio A. Mele, Sumeet Khatri, Lorenzo Leone, Jose Carrasco, Christian D. Marciniak, Ivan Pogorelov, Milena Guevara-Bertsch, Robert Freund, Rainer Blatt, Philipp Schindler, Thomas Monz, Martin Ringbauer, and Jens Eisert

This article shows that Rains’ quantum shadow enumerators, a powerful tool in quantum error correction, admit a direct physical interpretation in terms of outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements. This connection enables efficient learning protocols for these quantities and is demonstrated experimentally on a trapped-ion quantum device.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023318] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a physical interpretation of Rains' quantum shadow enumerators in terms of two-copy Bell measurements and demonstrates their efficient experimental measurement on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum shadow enumerators are powerful tools for analyzing quantum error-correcting codes, but they lack a direct physical interpretation and are difficult to measure experimentally.
method: The authors show that shadow enumerators correspond to outcome statistics of two-copy Bell measurements, enabling efficient learning protocols. They implement these protocols on a trapped-ion quantum device.
result: They experimentally extract shadow enumerators for small quantum codes, validating the theoretical connection and demonstrating the feasibility of the measurement scheme.
conclusion: The work bridges a gap between abstract enumerator theory and experimental quantum error correction, providing a practical tool for characterizing quantum codes.

title: Steady-state Entanglement Of Spin Qubits Mediated By Nonreciprocal And Chiral Magnons
authors: Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, And Silvia Viola Kusminskiy
abstract:
Author(s): Martijn Dols, Mikhail Cherkasskii, Victor A. S. V. Bittencourt, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero, Durga B. R. Dasari, and Silvia Viola Kusminskiy

We propose a hybrid quantum system in which a magnet supporting nonreciprocal magnons, chiral magnons, or both mediates the dissipative and unidirectional coupling of spin qubits. By driving the qubits, the steady state of this qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state. …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023310] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system using nonreciprocal and chiral magnons in a magnet to mediate dissipative, unidirectional coupling of spin qubits, achieving steady-state Bell state entanglement.
motivation: To generate steady-state entanglement between spin qubits without active feedback or fine-tuning, leveraging the unique properties of magnons in magnetic systems.
method: The system couples spin qubits to a magnet supporting nonreciprocal or chiral magnons; driving the qubits leads to dissipative coupling that steers the system into a maximally entangled Bell state.
result: The steady state of the qubit-qubit coupling scheme becomes the maximally entangled Bell state, enabled by the nonreciprocal/chiral magnon-mediated interaction.
conclusion: This hybrid platform offers a robust method for generating entanglement, relevant for quantum networking and information processing.

title: Geometric Decomposition Of Information Flow: New Insights Into Information Thermodynamics
authors: Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, And Sosuke Ito
abstract:
Author(s): Yoh Maekawa, Ryuna Nagayama, Kohei Yoshimura, and Sosuke Ito

We propose a decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite systems described by Markov jump processes. We introduce this decomposition using the geometric structure of probability currents and the conjugate thermodynamic forces. The housekeeping c…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023292] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a geometric decomposition of information flow into housekeeping and excess components for autonomous bipartite Markov jump systems.
motivation: To understand the thermodynamic role of information flow in autonomous bipartite systems beyond the conventional decomposition of entropy production.
method: Uses the geometric structure of probability currents and conjugate thermodynamic forces to decompose information flow into housekeeping and excess parts.
result: Derives a refined second law and fluctuation theorems for each component, showing that the housekeeping information flow is non-negative and the excess part obeys an integral fluctuation theorem.
conclusion: The decomposition provides new insights into the thermodynamics of information processing in autonomous systems, linking information flow to thermodynamic efficiency.

title: Long-range Photonic Device-independent Quantum Key Distribution Using Spontaneous Parametric Down-conversion Sources And Linear Optics
authors: Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, And Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto
abstract:
Author(s): Morteza Moradi, Maryam Afsary, Piotr Mironowicz, Enky Oudot, and Magdalena Stobińska-Moretto

We address the question of the implementation of long-distance device-independent quantum key distribution (DI QKD) by proposing two experimentally viable schemes. Those schemes use only spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optics. They achieve favorable key rate scaling proport…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023290] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: Proposes two experimentally viable DI QKD schemes using SPDC sources and linear optics that achieve favorable key rate scaling over long distances.
motivation: Device-independent QKD offers security without trusting devices, but long-distance implementations are challenging; the authors aim to design practical schemes with realistic components.
method: The schemes employ spontaneous parametric down-conversion sources and linear optical elements, analyzed using the entropy accumulation theorem for finite-size security.
result: The proposed schemes achieve key rates scaling proportionally to the square of the channel transmittance, enabling long-range DI QKD.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that DI QKD over long distances is feasible with current technology, bridging the gap between theory and experiment.

title: Coarse-grained Quantum Thermodynamics: Observation-dependent Quantities, Observation-independent Laws
authors: Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, And Gonzalo Manzano
abstract:
Author(s): Giulia Rubino, Časlav Brukner, and Gonzalo Manzano

In both classical and quantum thermodynamics, physical quantities are typically assigned objective values defined independently of our observations. We then refer to the “work performed by a gas,” or the “entropy of the gas,” regardless of how they are evaluated. Here, we question this conception in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023284] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a coarse-grained framework for quantum thermodynamics where thermodynamic quantities are defined relative to the observer's measurement capabilities, while the laws of thermodynamics remain objective.
motivation: Standard thermodynamics assumes objective values for quantities like work and entropy, but in quantum systems, these depend on measurement context. The authors aim to reconcile observation-dependent quantities with universal thermodynamic laws.
method: They develop a coarse-graining approach based on the observer's measurement resolution, defining effective thermodynamic variables that depend on the coarse-graining scale, and derive fluctuation theorems and second laws that hold for any coarse-graining.
result: The framework yields observation-dependent work and entropy, yet the second law and fluctuation theorems remain valid for all coarse-grainings, showing that thermodynamic laws are robust while quantities are context-dependent.
conclusion: Coarse-grained thermodynamics provides a consistent way to handle observer-dependence in quantum thermodynamics, with potential implications for quantum engines and information processing.

title: Testing The Problem Of Time With Cold Atoms
abstract:
Author(s): Giovanni Barontini

An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained miniuniverse to show that time can be defined without an external clock. It’s demonstrated that entropy exchange between different sectors of the system provides an internal time that robustly orders the dynamics and yields a Schrödinger description of the observed evolution.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022047] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: An ultracold atomic gas is used as a self-contained universe to show that entropy exchange between sectors provides an internal time, yielding a Schrödinger description without an external clock.
motivation: The problem of time in quantum mechanics and cosmology questions how time emerges from a timeless fundamental theory. This work aims to test whether entropy can serve as an internal time variable.
method: A cold atomic gas is prepared in a controlled state and its dynamics are observed. Entropy exchange between different sectors of the system is measured and used to define an internal time ordering.
result: The entropy-based internal time robustly orders the dynamics and reproduces a Schrödinger-like evolution, demonstrating that time can be defined without an external clock.
conclusion: The experiment supports the idea that time can emerge from thermodynamic entropy exchange, linking information thermodynamics to fundamental physics.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To provide a clear operational boundary between classical and nonclassical processes, recovering standard quantum signatures while identifying new quantum resources.
method: Develops a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: The rule recovers many known quantum signatures and shows that certain phenomena (e.g., some types of discord) are intrinsically quantum, contrary to prior belief.
conclusion: The work refines the classical-quantum boundary and suggests new avenues for quantum technology by exploiting previously overlooked quantum features.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn cavity noise into a resource for robust entanglement stabilization.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme to create and reconfigure entangled states, including spin-squeezed states and topological states.
result: They show that the dissipative approach can generate steady-state entanglement with high fidelity, and demonstrate reconfigurability by tuning external parameters, enabling applications in quantum sensing beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: The work provides a scalable platform for generating and controlling multipartite entanglement in hybrid spin-cavity systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss at breakeven using continuous drives, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors. Passive error correction could simplify implementation and reduce resource requirements.
method: The authors implement a passive error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect a qubit encoded in a bosonic mode against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: They demonstrate error correction at the breakeven point, where the corrected qubit lifetime exceeds the lifetime of the uncorrected physical qubit, marking a milestone in passive QEC.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction can achieve breakeven, showing potential for simpler and more efficient error correction in quantum computing.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times in monitored quantum dynamics, revealing scaling laws of quantum information lifetime.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information survives in open or monitored systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication, especially in the presence of noise and measurements.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are frequent enough, contrasting with the typical exponential decay in unmonitored systems.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements can act as a resource to protect quantum information, offering a strategy to improve the performance of near-term quantum devices.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation causes correlated phase error bursts in superconducting qubits, challenging quantum error correction even with radiation shielding.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing with superconducting qubits.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They identify a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists despite state-of-the-art radiation protection, with significant impact on error correction performance.
conclusion: Radiation-induced correlated phase errors pose a fundamental challenge for superconducting qubit arrays, requiring novel mitigation strategies beyond conventional shielding.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with linear experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networks but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable method to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using global driving fields and optical heralding to entangle spin emitters with inhomogeneous properties, leveraging spin-photon interfaces and cavity enhancement.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with overhead scaling linearly in qubit number, achieving up to 100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path to scalable quantum matter using inhomogeneous spin ensembles, relevant for quantum networking and computing.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity QED model with Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: To understand how kinetic constraints and long-range interactions in cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays give rise to exotic non-equilibrium phases.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay of cavity-mediated interactions and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They find blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars, demonstrating that kinetic constraints can stabilize ferromagnetic order and non-thermalizing states.
conclusion: Cavity QED with Rydberg atoms provides a platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and long-range quantum scars.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Proposes hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric tree-codes for quantum repeaters to improve resource efficiency and loss tolerance.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code schemes are resource-intensive and not optimized for near-term hardware.
method: Develops a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and introduces asymmetric code geometries tailored to lossy channels.
result: The optimized codes significantly reduce resource requirements (e.g., number of emitters, time steps) while maintaining high entanglement distribution rates under realistic loss.
conclusion: The proposed approach enhances the feasibility of quantum repeaters with current technology, advancing practical quantum networks.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Deep spin defects in ZnO are shown to have long coherence times and high-fidelity single-shot readout, making ZnO a promising platform for scalable quantum technologies.
motivation: Finding new solid-state platforms with long-lived spin qubits and high readout fidelity is crucial for scalable quantum computing and networking.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of deep-level defects in ZnO, measuring electron-phonon coupling, spin coherence time, and spin selectivity.
result: A deep defect in ZnO exhibits an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity enabling single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are viable new platforms for quantum technologies, offering competitive performance for spin qubits.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD, providing a rigorous framework for standards and certification.
motivation: Current security proofs often assume ideal devices or worst-case scenarios, which can be overly conservative or impractical. A method to integrate realistic device characterization into security proofs is needed for practical QKD certification.
method: The authors develop a general framework that takes device characterization data (e.g., from calibration or tomography) and translates it into constraints used in entropy-based security proofs, leveraging the entropy accumulation theorem.
result: The framework yields composable security bounds that are tighter than worst-case assumptions while remaining rigorous, enabling practical certification of QKD devices with realistic imperfections.
conclusion: This work bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and experimental implementations, providing a path toward standardized certification of QKD systems.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can enable more efficient error correction.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement a dispersive readout scheme to detect parity changes, thereby identifying erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion significantly boosts effective coherence times by allowing detection and removal of dominant relaxation errors.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to fault-tolerant quantum computing by turning relaxation errors into detectable erasures.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is central to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that leverages Fourier analysis over Abelian groups to solve the state hidden subgroup problem efficiently.
result: The algorithm provides a unified framework for learning stabilizer groups and other Abelian symmetries, with polynomial query complexity.
conclusion: This work advances quantum information theory by providing a general algorithmic primitive for symmetry learning, with implications for quantum error correction and cryptography.

title: Mode Multiplexing For Scalable Cavity-Enhanced Operations In Neutral-Atom Arrays
authors: Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Ziv Aqua, Matthew L. Peters, David C. Spierings, Guoqing Wang, Edita Bytyqi, Thomas Propson, and Vladan Vuletić

Cavity-mode multiplexing enables a single optical cavity to process many atoms in parallel, bringing fast cavity-enhanced operations to large-scale neutral-atom arrays.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020334] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for multiplexing cavity modes to enable parallel cavity-enhanced operations on many atoms in neutral-atom arrays.
motivation: Scalable neutral-atom quantum computing requires fast, high-fidelity operations on many qubits; cavity enhancement offers strong atom-photon coupling but is typically limited to single atoms.
method: The authors propose using multiple transverse cavity modes, each addressing a different atom or group of atoms, to parallelize cavity-enhanced operations across a large array.
result: Theoretical analysis shows that mode multiplexing can support hundreds of atoms with high cooperativity and low crosstalk, enabling parallel gate operations and state readout.
conclusion: Mode multiplexing provides a practical path to scale cavity-enhanced quantum operations to large neutral-atom arrays, advancing hybrid quantum systems for quantum computing.

title: Above 99.9% Fidelity Single-Qubit Gates, Two-Qubit Gates, And Readout In A Single Superconducting Quantum Device
abstract:
Author(s): Fabian Marxer et al.

Careful tuning of qubit-coupler interactions and a new calibration protocol enable simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates, controlled-
[PRX Quantum 7, 020333] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in a single superconducting quantum device through careful tuning and a new calibration protocol.
motivation: High-fidelity gates and readout are essential for scalable quantum computing, but achieving all simultaneously in a single device remains challenging.
method: The authors optimize qubit-coupler interactions and develop a new calibration protocol to minimize errors across all operations.
result: They achieve >99.9% fidelity for single-qubit gates, two-qubit gates, and readout in the same superconducting device.
conclusion: This work demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity operations are feasible, advancing the path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Spectral Properties And Coding Transitions Of Haar-Random Quantum Codes
authors: Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, And Sarang Gopalakrishnan
abstract:
Author(s): Grace M. Sommers, J. Alexander Jacoby, Zack Weinstein, David A. Huse, and Sarang Gopalakrishnan

An investigation of Haar-random quantum codes reveals a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases of quantum codes under local noise.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020328] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates Haar-random quantum codes and identifies a simple mechanism for the transition between decodable and nondecodable phases under local noise.
motivation: Understanding the robustness of quantum error-correcting codes against local noise is crucial for practical quantum computing. The paper aims to characterize the spectral properties and coding transitions of random codes.
method: The authors analyze Haar-random quantum codes using random matrix theory and statistical physics methods, studying the spectral properties of the code's density matrices and the decoding transition.
result: They find a sharp transition between decodable and nondecodable phases as a function of noise strength, with the transition point determined by the code's spectral properties.
conclusion: The work provides a simple, universal mechanism for the decoding transition in random quantum codes, offering insights into the design of practical error-correcting codes.

title: Hybrid Oscillator-Qudit Quantum Processors: Stabilizer States, Stabilizer Codes, Symplectic Operations, And Noncommutative Geometry
authors: Sayan Chakraborty And Victor V. Albert
abstract:
Author(s): Sayan Chakraborty and Victor V. Albert

Combinations of discrete- and continuous-variable systems are brought into the stabilizer formalism with new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes and could improve displacement sensing protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020320] Published Fri May 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the stabilizer formalism to hybrid systems combining discrete-variable (qudits) and continuous-variable (oscillator) degrees of freedom, introducing new stabilizer states, codes, and symplectic operations.
motivation: Hybrid oscillator-qudit systems are promising for quantum information processing, but a unified stabilizer formalism was lacking. The authors aim to provide a theoretical framework for such hybrid processors.
method: The authors develop a stabilizer formalism for hybrid systems using noncommutative geometry and symplectic operations over a ring, generalizing standard stabilizer codes to encompass both discrete and continuous variables.
result: They construct new classes of stabilizer states and scalable error-correcting codes tailored to hybrid systems, and show potential improvements in displacement sensing protocols.
conclusion: The work establishes a foundational framework for hybrid quantum processors, enabling systematic design of error correction and sensing protocols in these systems.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging stochastic thermodynamics and macroscopic thermodynamics using large deviations theory, providing a consistent fluctuation framework for nonequilibrium systems.
motivation: To unify mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with deterministic macroscopic laws, addressing inconsistencies in traditional Langevin approaches for far-from-equilibrium systems.
method: Uses large deviations theory to derive fluctuation theorems and thermodynamic principles from Markov jump processes, applied to chemical reaction networks, electronic circuits, and Potts models.
result: Establishes a thermodynamically consistent framework that preserves fluctuation theorems at macroscopic scales and elucidates rare fluctuations and attractor transitions.
conclusion: Provides a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines, directly relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information thermodynamics.

title: Active Quantum Reservoir Engineering: Using A Qubit To Manipulate Its Environment
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2143 (2026).

Quantum reservoir engineering leverages dissipative processes to achieve desired behaviour, with applications ranging from entanglement generation to quantum error correction. Therein, a structured environment acts as an entropy sink for the system and no time-dependent control over the system is required. We develop a theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering, where time-dependent control over a quantum system is used to manipulate its environment. In this case, the system may act as an entropy sink for the environment. Our framework captures the dynamical interplay between system and environment, and provides an intuitive picture of how finite-size effects and system-environment correlations allow for manipulating the environment by repeated initialisation of the quantum system. We illustrate our results with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to an environment of two-level systems and a semiconducting quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins. In both scenarios, we find qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, illustrating how active control can unlock new functionalities in open quantum systems.

.
tldr: A theoretical framework for active reservoir engineering where time-dependent control of a qubit manipulates its environment, demonstrated with superconducting and semiconducting platforms.
motivation: Standard quantum reservoir engineering uses a structured environment as an entropy sink, but active control can unlock new functionalities by allowing the system to manipulate its environment.
method: Develops a theoretical framework capturing the dynamical interplay between system and environment, including finite-size effects and correlations, and illustrates with two examples: a superconducting qubit coupled to two-level systems and a quantum dot coupled to nuclear spins.
result: Qualitative agreement with previous experimental results, showing that repeated initialization of the quantum system can manipulate the environment.
conclusion: Active control in open quantum systems enables new functionalities for quantum information processing, with potential applications in quantum error correction and entanglement generation.

title: Decoupling Local Classicality From Classical Explainability: A Noncontextual Model For Bilocal Classical Theory And A Locally-classical But Contextual Theory
authors: Sina Soltani, Marco Erba, David Schmid, And John H.selby
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2142 (2026).

We construct an ontological model for the theory known as bilocal classical theory [1]. To our knowledge, this is only the second time that an ontological model has been constructed for an entire theory, rather than just for some particular scenarios within a theory. This result refutes a conjecture from [1] which suggested that there might be no local-realist ontological model for bilocal classical theory. Moreover, it is the first time that an ontological model has been constructed for a theory that fails to be locally tomographic, showing that the assumption of local tomography underpinning the structure theorem in [2] is a genuine limitation of the theorem. This demonstrates that in general there is no tension between failures of local tomography and classical explainability (i.e., generalised noncontextuality). In fact, bilocal classical theory is in many ways more simply understood via the underlying ontological model than it is within its original formulation (much as how odd-dimensional stabiliser subtheories can be more simply understood via Spekkens' toy theory). Furthermore, this result naturally leads to the question, does every locally-classical theory admit of an ontological model? By constructing a concrete counterexample, we show that this is not the case. Our findings demonstrate that there is no straightforward relationship between theories being locally-classical, and them being classically-explainable. This shows that the fundamental status of compositional properties (such as local tomography) is not a technical side-issue, but a central and unavoidable question for a coherent understanding even of classicality itself.

.
tldr: Constructs an ontological model for bilocal classical theory, refuting a conjecture and showing that local classicality does not imply classical explainability.
motivation: To understand the relationship between local tomography, local classicality, and classical explainability (generalized noncontextuality) in ontological models.
method: Constructs an explicit ontological model for bilocal classical theory using a hidden variable framework, and then builds a counterexample theory that is locally classical but contextual.
result: Bilocal classical theory admits a local-realist ontological model despite failing local tomography, and there exists a locally-classical theory that is contextual.
conclusion: Local classicality and classical explainability are independent properties; compositional properties like local tomography are central to understanding classicality.

title: Measurement Incompatibility And Quantum Steering Via Linear Programming
authors: Lucas E. A. Porto, Sébastien Designolle, Sebastian Pokutta, And Marco Túlio Quintino
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2141 (2026).

The problem of deciding whether a set of quantum measurements is jointly measurable is known to be equivalent to determining whether a quantum assemblage is unsteerable. This problem can be formulated as a semidefinite program (SDP). However, the number of variables and constraints in such a formulation grows exponentially with the number of measurements, rendering it intractable for large measurement sets. In this work, we circumvent this problem by transforming the SDP into a hierarchy of linear programs that compute upper and lower bounds on the incompatibility robustness with a complexity that grows polynomially in the number of measurements. The hierarchy is guaranteed to converge and it can be applied to arbitrary measurements – including non-projective POVMs (Positive Operator-Valued Measures) – in arbitrary dimensions. While convergence becomes impractical in high dimensions, in the case of qubits our method reliably provides accurate upper and lower bounds for the incompatibility robustness of sets with several hundred measurements in a short time using a standard laptop. We also apply our methods to qutrits, obtaining non-trivial upper and lower bounds in scenarios that are otherwise intractable using the standard SDP approach, although such bounds are significantly looser than the ones obtained in the qubit case. Finally, we show how our methods can be used to construct local hidden state models for states (i.e., to prove that a state cannot lead to steering under any possible local measurements), or conversely, to certify that a given state exhibits steering; for two-qubit quantum states, our approach is comparable to, and in some cases outperforms, the current best methods.

.
tldr: This paper transforms the SDP for joint measurability and steering into a hierarchy of linear programs, enabling efficient computation of incompatibility robustness for large measurement sets.
motivation: The standard SDP for deciding joint measurability and steering scales exponentially with the number of measurements, making it intractable for large sets. The authors aim to develop a more efficient method.
method: They reformulate the SDP as a hierarchy of linear programs that provide upper and lower bounds on incompatibility robustness, with polynomial complexity in the number of measurements. The hierarchy converges and applies to arbitrary POVMs.
result: For qubits, the method reliably bounds incompatibility robustness for hundreds of measurements quickly on a laptop. For qutrits, it yields non-trivial bounds where SDP is intractable. It also constructs local hidden state models or certifies steering for two-qubit states.
conclusion: The linear programming hierarchy offers a practical tool for analyzing measurement incompatibility and quantum steering in large measurement scenarios, outperforming standard SDP approaches in scalability.

title: Tight Bounds For Quantum Phase Estimation And Related Problems
authors: Nikhil S. Mande And Ronald de Wolf
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2140 (2026).

Phase estimation, due to Kitaev [17], is one of the most fundamental subroutines in quantum computing. In the basic scenario, one is given black-box access to a unitary [MATH], and an eigenstate [MATH] of [MATH] with unknown eigenvalue [MATH], and the task is to estimate the eigenphase [MATH] within [MATH], with high probability. The cost of an algorithm for us is the number of applications of [MATH] and [MATH]. We tightly characterize the cost of several variants of phase estimation where we are no longer given an eigenstate, but are required to estimate the maximum eigenphase of [MATH], aided by advice in the form of states (or a unitary preparing those states) which are promised to have at least a certain overlap [MATH] with the top eigenspace. We give algorithms and nearly matching lower bounds for all ranges of parameters. We show that a small number of copies of the advice state (or of an advice-preparing unitary) are not significantly better than having no advice at all. We also show that having lots of advice (applications of the advice-preparing unitary) does not significantly reduce cost, and neither does knowledge of the eigenbasis of [MATH]. We immediately obtain a lower bound on the complexity of the Unitary recurrence time problem, resolving an open question of She and Yuen [29]. Lastly, we study how efficiently one can reduce the error probability in the basic phase-estimation scenario. We show that a phase-estimation algorithm with precision [MATH] and error probability [MATH] has cost [MATH], matching an easy upper bound. This contrasts with some other scenarios in quantum computing (e.g., search) where error-probability reduction costs only a factor [MATH]. Our lower bound uses a variant of the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials.

.
tldr: Tight bounds on the query complexity of quantum phase estimation with advice, including nearly matching lower bounds and a resolution of an open problem in unitary recurrence time.
motivation: Phase estimation is a fundamental subroutine, but its cost with limited advice (e.g., copies of an eigenstate or a unitary preparing it) was not well understood. The authors aim to characterize the exact trade-offs between advice and query complexity.
method: The paper uses the polynomial method with trigonometric polynomials to prove lower bounds, and provides explicit algorithms that nearly match these bounds for all parameter regimes.
result: They show that a small number of advice copies are not significantly better than no advice, and that many advice applications do not reduce cost much. They also prove that error-probability reduction costs a factor of 1/ε, unlike search problems.
conclusion: The work tightly characterizes the complexity of phase estimation variants, resolving an open question about unitary recurrence time and providing a complete picture of the role of advice in this setting.

title: Qudit Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt Inequality And Nonlocality From Wigner Negativity
authors: Uta Isabella Meyer, Ivan Šupić, Damian Markham, And Frédéric Grosshans
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2139 (2026).

Nonlocality is an essential concept that distinguishes quantum from classical models and has been extensively studied in systems of qubits. For higher-dimensional systems, certain results for their two-level counterpart, like Bell violations with stabilizer states and Clifford operators, do not generalize. On the other hand, similar to continuous variable systems, Wigner negativity is necessary for nonlocality in qudit systems. We propose a new generalization of the CHSH inequality for qudits by inquiring correlations related to the Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under the adjoint action of a generalization of the qubit [MATH]-gate. A specified stabilizer state maximally violates the inequality among all qudit states based on its Wigner negativity. The Bell operator not only serves as a measure for the singlet fraction but also quantifies the volume of Wigner negativity. Additionally, we show how a bipartite entangled qudit state can serve as a witness for contextuality when it exhibits Wigner negativity. Furthermore, we identify rational-phase diagonal unitaries as the key resource that exactly reproduce the CGLMP and SATWAP violation with the maximally entangled state through simple phase-difference alignment.

.
tldr: Proposes a qudit CHSH inequality based on Wigner negativity of stabilizer states, showing maximal violation tied to Wigner negativity and linking nonlocality to contextuality.
motivation: Generalizing Bell inequalities to higher-dimensional systems is challenging because qubit results do not directly extend; understanding nonlocality in qudits is essential for quantum information.
method: Introduces a new CHSH inequality for qudits using correlations derived from Wigner negativity of stabilizer states under a generalized π/8 gate, and analyzes the Bell operator's relation to singlet fraction and Wigner negativity volume.
result: A specific stabilizer state achieves maximal violation among all qudit states, and the Bell operator quantifies both singlet fraction and Wigner negativity; bipartite entangled qudit states with Wigner negativity witness contextuality.
conclusion: Wigner negativity is a key resource for nonlocality in qudit systems, and the proposed inequality provides a practical tool for detecting nonlocality and contextuality.

title: Quantum Thermodynamics Of The Caldeira-Leggett Model With Non-equilibrium Gaussian Reservoirs
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2136 (2026).

We introduce a non-equilibrium version of the Caldeira-Leggett model in which a quantum particle is strongly coupled to a set of engineered reservoirs. The reservoirs are composed by collections of squeezed and displaced thermal modes, in contrast to the standard case in which the modes are assumed to be at equilibrium. The model proves to be very versatile. Strongly displaced/squeezed reservoirs can be used to generate an effective time dependence in the system Hamiltonian and can be identified as sources of pure work. In the case of squeezing, the time dependence is stochastic and breaks the fluctuation-dissipation relation, this can be reconciled with the second law of thermodynamics by correctly accounting for the energy used to generate the initial non-equilibrium conditions. To go beyond the average description and compute the full heat statistics, we treat squeezing and displacement as generalized Hamiltonians on a modified Keldysh contour. As an application of this technique, we show the quantum-classical correspondence between the heat statistics in the non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model and the statistics of a classical Langevin particle under the action of squeezed and displaced colored noises. Finally, we discuss thermodynamic symmetries of the heat generating function, proving a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance and showing that the conservation of energy at the trajectory level emerges in the classical limit.

.
tldr: Extends the Caldeira-Leggett model to non-equilibrium Gaussian reservoirs, deriving thermodynamic statistics and fluctuation theorems for a strongly coupled quantum particle.
motivation: To understand quantum thermodynamics beyond the weak-coupling and equilibrium-reservoir assumptions, and to model engineered reservoirs that can act as work sources.
method: Introduces squeezed and displaced thermal reservoirs, treats them via a modified Keldysh contour, and computes full heat statistics using generalized Hamiltonians.
result: Derives a fluctuation theorem for the energy balance, shows quantum-classical correspondence in heat statistics, and clarifies how the second law is maintained despite broken fluctuation-dissipation relation.
conclusion: The non-equilibrium Caldeira-Leggett model provides a versatile framework for studying quantum thermodynamics with strong coupling and engineered reservoirs, with potential applications to quantum heat engines and work extraction.

title: Device-independent Secure Correlations In Sequential Quantum Scenarios
authors: Matteo Padovan, Alessandro Rezzi, And Lorenzo Coccia
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2131 (2026).

Device-independent quantum information is attracting significant attention, particularly for its applications in information security. This interest arises because the security of device-independent protocols relies solely on the observed outcomes of spatially separated measurements and the validity of quantum physics. Sequential scenarios, i.e., where measurements occur in a precise temporal order, have been proved to enhance performance of device-independent protocols in some specific cases by enabling the reuse of the same quantum state. In this work, we propose a systematic approach to designing sequential quantum protocols for device-independent security. Our method begins with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol and transforms it into a sequential protocol by replacing one measurement with its non-projective counterpart and adding an additional user thereafter. We analytically prove that, with this systematic construction, the resulting ideal correlations are secure in the sense that they cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, thereby enabling, for example, the device-independent certification of all the randomness present in the observed correlations. The general recipe we provide can be exploited for further development of new device-independent quantum schemes for security.

.
tldr: A systematic method to construct device-independent sequential quantum protocols from bipartite self-testing qubit protocols, ensuring secure correlations.
motivation: Device-independent protocols offer security based solely on observed correlations, and sequential scenarios can enhance performance by reusing quantum states; a general construction method was lacking.
method: The authors start with a bipartite self-testing qubit protocol, replace one measurement with a non-projective counterpart, and add an additional user to obtain a sequential protocol; they prove analytically that the resulting correlations are secure.
result: The constructed ideal correlations cannot be reproduced as a statistical mixture of other correlations, enabling device-independent certification of all randomness in the observed correlations.
conclusion: The general recipe provides a systematic way to develop new device-independent quantum schemes for security in sequential scenarios.

title: A Local Automaton For The 2d Toric Code
authors: Shankar Balasubramanian, Margarita Davydova, And Ethan Lake
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2125 (2026).

We construct a local decoder for the 2D toric code using ideas from the hierarchical classical cellular automata of Tsirelson and Gács. Our decoder is a circuit of strictly local quantum operations preserving a logical state for exponential time in the presence of circuit-level noise without the need for non-local classical computation or communication. Our construction is not translation invariant in spacetime, but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks of 2D toric codes. This solves the open problem of constructing a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions.

.
tldr: Constructs a local decoder for the 2D toric code that preserves logical state for exponential time under circuit-level noise without non-local classical computation.
motivation: Open problem: building a local topological quantum memory in fewer than four dimensions. Existing decoders require non-local classical processing.
method: Uses ideas from hierarchical classical cellular automata (Tsirelson and Gács) to design a strictly local quantum circuit decoder for the 2D toric code.
result: The decoder achieves exponential memory time under circuit-level noise, is not translation invariant in spacetime but can be made time-translation invariant in 3D with stacks.
conclusion: Solves the open problem of a local topological quantum memory below four dimensions, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: A Refined Frauchiger–Renner Paradox Based On Strong Contextuality
authors: Laurens Walleghem, Rui Soares Barbosa, Matthew F. Pusey, And Stefan Weigert
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2116 (2026).

The Frauchiger–Renner paradox derives an inconsistency when quantum theory is used to describe the use of itself, by means of a scenario where agents model other agents quantumly and reason about each other's knowledge. We observe that logical contextuality (à la Hardy) is the key ingredient of the FR paradox, and we provide a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario. In contrast to the FR paradox, this GHZ–FR paradox neither requires post-selection nor any reasoning by observers who are modelled quantumly. If one accepts the universality of quantum theory including superobservers, we propose a natural extension of Peres's dictum to resolve these extended Wigner's friend paradoxes.

.
tldr: The paper strengthens the Frauchiger–Renner paradox using strong contextuality from the GHZ–Mermin scenario, eliminating the need for post-selection or quantum self-modeling.
motivation: To resolve inconsistencies in quantum theory when describing itself, and to clarify the role of contextuality in extended Wigner's friend scenarios.
method: The authors identify logical contextuality as the key ingredient of the original FR paradox and construct a stronger paradox based on the strongly contextual GHZ–Mermin scenario.
result: The GHZ–FR paradox is stronger than the original, requiring no post-selection or quantum reasoning by agents, and is resolved by extending Peres's dictum.
conclusion: Strong contextuality underlies the FR paradox, and the new paradox provides a cleaner foundation for discussing the consistency of quantum theory.

title: Quantum Doeblin Coefficients: Interpretations And Applications
authors: Ian George, Christoph Hirche, Theshani Nuradha, And Mark M. Wilde
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2115 (2026).

In classical information theory, the Doeblin coefficient of a classical channel provides an efficiently computable upper bound on the total-variation contraction coefficient of the channel, leading to what is known as a strong data-processing inequality. Here, we investigate quantum Doeblin coefficients as a generalization of the classical concept. In particular, we define various new quantum Doeblin coefficients, one of which has several desirable properties, including concatenation and multiplicativity, in addition to being efficiently computable. We also develop various interpretations of two of the quantum Doeblin coefficients, including representations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, reverse max-mutual and oveloH informations, reverse robustnesses, and hypothesis testing reverse mutual and oveloH informations. Our interpretations of quantum Doeblin coefficients as either entanglement-assisted or unassisted exclusion values are particularly appealing, indicating that they are proportional to the best possible error probabilities one could achieve in state-exclusion tasks by making use of the channel. We also outline various applications of quantum Doeblin coefficients, ranging from limitations on quantum machine learning algorithms that use parameterized quantum circuits (noise-induced barren plateaus), on error mitigation protocols, on the sample complexity of noisy quantum hypothesis testing, on the fairness of noisy quantum models, and on mixing, indistinguishability, and decoupling times of time-varying channels. All of these applications make use of the fact that quantum Doeblin coefficients appear in upper bounds on various trace-distance contraction coefficients of a quantum channel. Furthermore, in all of these applications, our analysis using quantum Doeblin coefficients provides improvements of various kinds over contributions from prior literature, both in terms of generality and being efficiently computable.

.
tldr: This paper generalizes classical Doeblin coefficients to quantum channels, providing efficiently computable upper bounds on trace-distance contraction and demonstrating applications in quantum machine learning, error mitigation, and hypothesis testing.
motivation: Classical Doeblin coefficients yield strong data-processing inequalities; a quantum analog is needed to bound contraction coefficients of quantum channels and enable applications in quantum information theory.
method: The authors define several quantum Doeblin coefficients, prove properties like concatenation and multiplicativity, and derive interpretations as minimal singlet fractions, exclusion values, and reverse mutual informations.
result: Quantum Doeblin coefficients provide efficiently computable upper bounds on trace-distance contraction, improving prior bounds in applications such as noise-induced barren plateaus, error mitigation, and sample complexity of hypothesis testing.
conclusion: Quantum Doeblin coefficients are a versatile tool for bounding contraction of quantum channels, with broad applications in quantum information processing.

title: Resource Theory Of Interactive Quantum Instruments
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, And Paul Skrzypczyk
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh, Armin Tavakoli, Huan-Yu Ku, and Paul Skrzypczyk

Quantum instruments describe both the classical outcome and the updated quantum state in a measurement process. To do this in a nontrivial way, instruments must have the capability to interact coherently with the state that they measure. Here we develop a resource theory for instruments. We consider…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062445] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops a resource theory for quantum instruments, characterizing their ability to interact coherently with measured states.
motivation: Quantum instruments are fundamental in measurement theory, but their capabilities beyond classical outcomes are not well understood; a resource theory framework can quantify their non-classical features.
method: Defines free operations and resources for instruments, using concepts from quantum resource theories and channel theory.
result: Identifies a hierarchy of instrument resources, including coherence and entanglement, and provides measures to quantify them.
conclusion: The resource theory offers a systematic way to classify and compare quantum instruments, with implications for quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Miniature Work-to-work Converter Engine Powered By Motor Protein
authors: Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, And Sudipto Muhuri
abstract:
Author(s): Suraj Deshmukh, Sougata Guha, Basudha Roy, Shivprasad Patil, Arnab Saha, and Sudipto Muhuri
