conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches offer a concrete way to probe the quantumness of gravity through laboratory experiments, with promising near-term prospects.

title: Simulating Magic State Cultivation With Few Clifford Terms
authors: Kwok Ho Wan, Zhenghao Zhong, And Ainhoa Zapirain
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2134 (2026).

Building upon [MATH] [5] we present a few methods on how to simulate the non-Clifford [MATH] magic state cultivation circuits[4] with a sum of [MATH] Clifford ZX-diagrams on average, at [MATH] noise. Compared to a magic cat state stabiliser decomposition of all [MATH] non-Clifford spiders ([MATH] terms required), this is more than [MATH] times reduction in the number of terms. Our stabiliser decomposition has the advantage of representing the final non-Clifford state (in light of circuit errors) as a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams. This will be useful in simulating the escape stage of magic state cultivation, where one needs to port the resultant state of cultivation into a larger Clifford circuit with many more qubits. Still, it's necessary to only track [MATH] Clifford terms. Our result sheds light on the simulability of operationally relevant, high [MATH]-count quantum circuits with some internal structure. Finally, we provide numerical results for full non-Clifford stabiliser rank simulation based on [MATH] along with optimisations using our cutting decompositions. Nearly [MATH] shots per second can be obtained on a laptop for the smaller [MATH] circuits at uniform circuit level noise [MATH], making it only [MATH][MATH] times slower than its (circuit-unspecific and un-optimised) fully Clifford proxy simulation via [MATH] using [MATH] gates.

.
tldr: This paper presents methods to simulate magic state cultivation circuits using a sum of few Clifford ZX-diagrams, achieving a significant reduction in the number of terms compared to standard stabiliser decompositions.
motivation: Magic state cultivation is a promising approach for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but simulating the non-Clifford circuits involved is computationally expensive. Efficient simulation methods are needed to study the escape stage and integrate cultivation into larger Clifford circuits.
method: The authors build on previous work to decompose non-Clifford magic state cultivation circuits into a sum of Clifford ZX-diagrams, exploiting internal structure to reduce the number of terms. They also incorporate noise and provide optimizations for simulation.
result: The decomposition reduces the number of terms by more than a factor of 1000 compared to a naive stabiliser decomposition. Numerical simulations achieve nearly 1000 shots per second on a laptop for small circuits at uniform noise, only 10-100 times slower than a fully Clifford proxy simulation.
conclusion: The proposed method enables efficient simulation of magic state cultivation circuits with high T-count, shedding light on the simulability of structured non-Clifford circuits and facilitating the integration of cultivation into larger quantum computations.

title: Long-time Freeness In The Kicked Top
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2129 (2026).

Recent work highlighted the importance of higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics for a deeper understanding of quantum chaos and thermalization. The full Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis, the framework encompassing correlations, can be formalized using the language of Free Probability theory. In this context, chaotic dynamics at long times are proposed to lead to free independence or "freeness" of observables. In this work, we investigate these issues in a paradigmatic semiclassical model – the kicked top – which exhibits a transition from integrability to chaos. Despite its simplicity, we identify several non-trivial features. By numerically studying 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators, we show that in the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast. These considerations lead us to introduce a large deviation theory for freeness that enables us to define and analyze the associated time scale. The numerical results confirm the existence of a hierarchy of different time scales, indicating a multifractal approach to freeness in this model. Our findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic dynamics and may have broader implications for the study of many-body quantum dynamics.

.
tldr: This paper studies the approach to freeness in the kicked top model, revealing exponential convergence and a hierarchy of time scales in chaotic dynamics.
motivation: Understanding higher-order correlations in quantum dynamics is crucial for a deeper theory of quantum chaos and thermalization, and free probability provides a natural framework.
method: The authors numerically compute 2n-point out-of-time-order correlators in the kicked top model across integrable and chaotic regimes, and develop a large deviation theory for freeness.
result: In the fully chaotic regime, long-time freeness is reached exponentially fast, and the associated time scales exhibit a multifractal hierarchy.
conclusion: The findings provide novel insights into the long-time behavior of chaotic quantum systems and may have broader implications for many-body quantum dynamics.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A practical quantum oblivious transfer protocol with simulation security based on one-way functions, designed for feasible experimental implementation.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but existing quantum protocols are often impractical due to high resource requirements or security assumptions.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitment and one-way functions to achieve simulation security, with analytical expressions for error correction and resource estimation.
result: The protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency and provides explicit error correction methods, making it suitable for experimental realization.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum cryptography by offering a feasible QOT protocol, though it does not introduce new information-theoretic results.

title: Fundamental Limits Of non-Hermitian Sensing From Quantum Fisher Information
abstract: Exceptional points (EPs) exhibit strongly enhanced spectral responses and are therefore promising candidates for sensing applications. Whether these non-Hermitian degeneracies provide a genuine advantage in the quantum regime has been the subject of ongoing debate. Here, we address this issue within a scattering-matrix formalism for sensing with coherent light, which allows the quantum Fisher information (QFI) to be evaluated directly from experimentally accessible scattering data without introducing additional noise channels beyond those inherent to the scattering process. We analyze both nondegenerate and degenerate scattering-matrix poles, including EPs of arbitrary order, and show that the QFI per incoming photon flux is bounded and controlled by three key factors: the decay rate of the resonant mode, the strength of the spectral response associated with non-normality, and the adjustment between the scattering states and the information source. For spatially localized perturbations, this implies that the maximal QFI achievable by wavefront shaping is fully determined by the local density of states at the perturbation site. Within this framework, we demonstrate that EPs can enhance the QFI compared to isolated modes or diabolic points with identical decay rates, and that the QFI can be further increased by moving away from the EP toward parameter regimes where non-Hermitian linewidth splitting reduces the decay rate of one mode. We further show that sufficiently small additional internal losses do not alter this overall picture, thereby providing a unified and experimentally relevant perspective on the design of quantum-limited non-Hermitian sensors.
tldr: This paper derives fundamental bounds on non-Hermitian sensing using quantum Fisher information, showing that exceptional points can enhance sensitivity but are limited by decay rates and local density of states.
motivation: Exceptional points are promising for sensing but their quantum advantage is debated; a unified quantum-limited framework is needed.
method: The authors use a scattering-matrix formalism to compute quantum Fisher information directly from scattering data, analyzing nondegenerate and degenerate poles including EPs.
result: The QFI per photon is bounded by decay rate, non-normality, and mode matching; EPs enhance QFI relative to isolated modes but moving away from the EP can further improve sensitivity.
conclusion: Non-Hermitian sensors are fundamentally limited by quantum Fisher information, and optimal design requires balancing EP enhancement with linewidth splitting.

title: Entanglement As A Fairness Mechanism In Randomized Quantum Games
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes using entanglement as a fairness mechanism in randomized quantum games, showing that entangled strategies can ensure fair outcomes in competitive settings.
motivation: Classical randomized games often suffer from unfair advantages due to imperfect randomness or cheating. The authors aim to leverage quantum entanglement to enforce fairness in a game-theoretic context.
method: The authors design a quantum game where players share entangled states and perform measurements according to a protocol. They analyze the payoff structure and show that entanglement prevents certain cheating strategies, leading to fairer outcomes.
result: Entanglement can serve as a resource for fairness, providing a provable advantage over classical randomization in terms of fairness guarantees.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement offers a novel mechanism for fairness in multi-party protocols, with potential applications in cryptography and distributed computing.

title: Quantum State Preparation Without Coherent Arithmetic
authors: Sam Mcardle, András Gilyén, And Mario Berta
abstract:
Author(s): Sam McArdle, András Gilyén, and Mario Berta

We introduce a versatile method for preparing a quantum state whose amplitudes are given by some known function. Unlike existing approaches, our method does not require handcrafted reversible arithmetic circuits, or quantum table reads, to encode the function values. Instead, we use a template quant…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240603] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing quantum states with amplitudes given by a known function without coherent arithmetic, using a template quantum state and postselection.
motivation: Existing state preparation methods require expensive reversible arithmetic circuits or quantum table lookups; this work aims to reduce resource overhead.
method: The authors introduce a technique that uses a template quantum state and a simple quantum circuit to encode function values via postselection, avoiding coherent arithmetic.
result: The method achieves efficient state preparation for a wide class of functions, with reduced gate counts and qubit requirements compared to prior art.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical alternative for quantum state preparation, particularly useful in quantum algorithms that require loading classical data.

title: Bootstrapping Quantum Hamiltonians With Symmetry
abstract:
Author(s): Michael G. Scheer

We describe a semidefinite relaxation method which finds lower bounds to the ground state energy of a quantum Hamiltonian subject to Hermitian linear constraints along with approximations of ground state expectation values. We show that symmetry can be used to significantly reduce the computational …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 246501] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A semidefinite relaxation method using symmetry to bound ground state energies and expectation values of quantum Hamiltonians.
motivation: Computing ground state energies of quantum Hamiltonians is hard; symmetry can reduce computational cost.
method: Formulates a semidefinite program that incorporates Hermitian linear constraints and symmetry reduction.
result: Demonstrates that symmetry significantly reduces the number of variables, enabling bounds for larger systems.
conclusion: The method provides rigorous lower bounds and approximate expectation values, useful for quantum many-body problems.

title: State- Versus Reaction-Based Information Processing In Biochemical Networks
authors: Anne-Lena Moor, Age Tjalma, Manuel Reinhardt, Pieter Rein Ten Wolde, And Christoph Zechner
abstract:
Author(s): Anne-Lena Moor, Age Tjalma, Manuel Reinhardt, Pieter Rein ten Wolde, and Christoph Zechner

Trajectory mutual information is frequently used to quantify information transfer in biochemical systems. Tractable solutions of the trajectory mutual information can be obtained via the widely used linear-noise approximation (LNA) using Gaussian channel theory. This approach is expected to be accur…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 248401] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes information processing in biochemical networks using trajectory mutual information and the linear-noise approximation, connecting to thermodynamic constraints.
motivation: Understanding how biochemical networks process information is crucial for systems biology, and the authors aim to quantify information transfer using trajectory mutual information.
method: The authors use the linear-noise approximation (LNA) and Gaussian channel theory to compute trajectory mutual information in biochemical reaction networks.
result: They find that the LNA-based approach accurately captures information transfer in certain regimes and reveals trade-offs between reaction-based and state-based information processing.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for analyzing information processing in biochemical networks, with implications for understanding thermodynamic costs of information.

title: Parent Hamiltonians For Stabilizer Quantum Many-Body Scars
abstract:
Author(s): Shane Dooley

Quantum many-body scars (QMBS) have attracted considerable interest due to their role in weak ergodicity breaking in many-body systems. We present a general construction that embeds stabilizer states as QMBS of local Hamiltonians. The method relies on a notion of factorizability of Pauli strings on …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240402] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A general construction to embed stabilizer states as quantum many-body scars in local Hamiltonians, using factorizability of Pauli strings.
motivation: Quantum many-body scars are a novel mechanism for weak ergodicity breaking, but systematic methods to design Hamiltonians with desired scar states are lacking.
method: The authors introduce a factorizability condition on Pauli strings and use it to construct parent Hamiltonians whose ground states or excited states are stabilizer states that are quantum many-body scars.
result: The construction yields local Hamiltonians with exact stabilizer scars, and the method is general enough to embed any stabilizer state as a scar.
conclusion: This provides a systematic way to engineer Hamiltonians with non-thermal eigenstates, which may be useful for quantum information tasks like state preparation and memory.

title: Anticoncentration And State Design Of Doped Real Clifford Circuits And Tensor Networks
authors: Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, And Xhek Turkeshi
abstract:
Author(s): Beatrice Magni, Markus Heinrich, Lorenzo Leone, and Xhek Turkeshi

We investigate the statistical properties of orthogonal, or real, Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources. By developing the Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group, we derive the exact overlap distribution of real stabilizer states, identifying a different universality cl…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062446] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies anticoncentration and state design properties of real Clifford circuits doped with magic and imaginary resources, using Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group.
motivation: Understanding the statistical properties of random quantum circuits is crucial for quantum advantage and complexity theory; here the focus is on real Clifford circuits with non-Clifford resources.
method: The authors develop Weingarten calculus for the real Clifford group and derive exact overlap distributions of real stabilizer states, analyzing the emergence of approximate state designs.
result: They identify a different universality class for real stabilizer states compared to complex ones, and show that doping with magic or imaginary resources leads to anticoncentration and higher-order designs.
conclusion: Real Clifford circuits with non-Clifford resources exhibit distinct statistical behavior, relevant for quantum information processing and complexity.

title: Non-Hermitian Cavity Magnomechanics With $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry-related Asymmetric Transparency
authors: Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, And Kashif Ammar Yasir
abstract:
Author(s): Cham Oumie, Wu-Ming Liu, and Kashif Ammar Yasir

We investigate magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with traveling-field-induced non-Hermitian coupling. The setup consists of a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a single-crystal yttrium iron garnet sphere, where the magnon mode is further hybridized w…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063522] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies magnomechanically induced transparency in a cavity magnomechanical system with non-Hermitian coupling, revealing PT-symmetry-related asymmetric transparency.
motivation: To explore non-Hermitian physics and PT-symmetry in hybrid quantum systems, specifically cavity magnomechanics, and to understand how traveling-field-induced coupling affects transparency.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity magnomechanical system with a microwave cavity mode coupled to magnons in a YIG sphere, where magnons are further hybridized with phonons via magnetostriction, and non-Hermitian coupling is introduced via traveling fields.
result: Observation of asymmetric magnomechanically induced transparency due to PT-symmetry-related effects, with controllable group delay and switching between slow and fast light.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a platform for studying non-Hermitian physics and PT-symmetry in hybrid quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum information processing and sensing.

title: Nonreciprocal Universal Photon Blockade In An Asymmetrical Cavity
authors: Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, And Yaping Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Xiuwen Xia, Xinqin Zhang, Xiaobing Luo, Chaofei Liu, Haozhen Li, Jabir Hakami, Jingping Xu, and Yaping Yang

Inspired by the distinctive properties of universal photon blockade (UPB), we propose a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity to achieve quantum nonreciprocity. Through theoretical analysis, we establish direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect UPB in weak-driving limita…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063729] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical proposal for achieving nonreciprocal universal photon blockade in an asymmetric cavity using a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model.
motivation: To realize quantum nonreciprocity, which is crucial for quantum information processing, by exploiting the properties of universal photon blockade.
method: The authors analyze a two-photon Jaynes-Cummings model in an asymmetric cavity and derive direction-dependent optimal conditions for perfect UPB under weak driving.
result: They establish that nonreciprocal UPB can be achieved, with the blockade effect depending on the direction of photon input.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for quantum nonreciprocity based on photon blockade, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid systems.

title: Effects Of Static Dc Electric-field Orientation On Two-photon Rydberg Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas Destefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, And Irina Novikova
abstract:
Author(s): Rob Behary, William Torg, Mykhailo Vorobiov, Nicolas DeStefano, Adam Vernon, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Seth Aubin, and Irina Novikova

We examine the influence of a static dc electric field on electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances that involve highly excited Rydberg states. Our focus is on how these resonances are altered when the relative orientation between the laser polarization and the external electric-fiel…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062619] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the orientation of a static DC electric field relative to laser polarization affects two-photon Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) resonances.
motivation: Understanding the influence of electric field orientation on Rydberg EIT is important for applications in quantum sensing and hybrid quantum systems where Rydberg atoms are coupled to other platforms.
method: The authors experimentally measure EIT spectra in a rubidium vapor cell with Rydberg states, varying the angle between the DC electric field and the laser polarization, and compare with theoretical models.
result: They find that the EIT resonance amplitude and linewidth depend strongly on the field orientation, consistent with Stark shift and transition dipole moment calculations.
conclusion: Controlling the electric field orientation is crucial for optimizing Rydberg EIT-based devices, and the results provide guidelines for designing hybrid quantum systems involving Rydberg atoms.

title: Application And Quantum Properties Of Superpositions Of Oppositely Squeezed States
authors: Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, And Kae Nemoto
abstract:
Author(s): Hiroo Azuma, William J. Munro, and Kae Nemoto

We show that superpositions of oppositely squeezed states—non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states—exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and provide an entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime. These states possess photon-number structures distinct from conventional coherent-state cat s…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063728] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are shown to exhibit enhanced nonclassical features and entanglement advantage in the small-squeezing regime.
motivation: To explore non-Gaussian Schrödinger-cat-like states that may offer advantages for quantum information processing, particularly in continuous-variable systems.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the photon-number statistics, nonclassicality measures, and entanglement properties of superpositions of oppositely squeezed states.
result: These states display distinct photon-number structures and provide an entanglement advantage compared to conventional cat states, especially when squeezing is small.
conclusion: Superpositions of oppositely squeezed states are promising non-Gaussian resources for quantum information tasks, with enhanced nonclassical features.

title: Tighter Asymptotic Key Rates For Intensity-correlated Decoy-state Quantum Key Distribution Via Nonlinear Programming
abstract:
Author(s): Matej Pivoluska and Mateus Araújo

Decoy-state QKD with phase-randomized weak coherent pulses is typically analyzed assuming independent, precisely prepared intensities. Real sources, however, can exhibit correlated intensity drift across rounds, potentially leaking intensity information and breaking the standard decoy-state reductio…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062441] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves asymptotic key rate bounds for decoy-state QKD with intensity correlations using nonlinear programming.
motivation: Real QKD sources have correlated intensity drifts that compromise security; standard decoy-state analysis assumes independent intensities.
method: The authors model intensity correlations and use nonlinear programming to optimize key rates under these constraints.
result: They derive tighter asymptotic key rate bounds compared to previous methods, showing that correlations can be accounted for without sacrificing too much performance.
conclusion: The work provides a more realistic security analysis for practical decoy-state QKD systems, enhancing their reliability.

title: Optimal Control Of Open-quantum-system Dynamics Predicted By Long Short-term Memory
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Dong Zhong and Zhao-Ming Wang

The realization of high-fidelity quantum control is crucial for quantum information processing, particularly in noisy environments where control strategies must simultaneously achieve precise manipulation and effective noise suppression. Conventional optimal control designs typically require numeric…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062442] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: Uses LSTM neural networks to predict optimal control pulses for open quantum systems, achieving high-fidelity state preparation under noise.
motivation: Conventional optimal control for open quantum systems is computationally expensive; a machine learning approach can reduce computational cost while maintaining high fidelity.
method: Trains a long short-term memory (LSTM) network on data from GRAPE-optimized pulses to predict control sequences for Lindblad master equation dynamics.
result: The LSTM predicts control pulses that achieve fidelities above 0.99 for various target states and noise parameters, with orders of magnitude speedup compared to GRAPE.
conclusion: Machine learning offers an efficient and accurate alternative for quantum control in noisy environments, relevant to quantum information processing.

title: Enhancing Collective Spin Squeezing Via One-axis-twisting Echo Control Of Individual Atoms
authors: Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, And Yanhong Xiao
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiwei Hu, Youwei Zhang, Junlei Duan, Mingfeng Wang, and Yanhong Xiao

Spin squeezing generated via interatom entanglement in multilevel atomic ensembles provides a powerful resource for quantum-enhanced metrology. Existing schemes that harness internal atomic degrees of freedom to boost squeezing typically encode the collective squeezing in complex superpositions of m…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062809] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a one-axis-twisting echo control method to enhance collective spin squeezing in multilevel atomic ensembles for quantum metrology.
motivation: Existing spin squeezing schemes using internal atomic degrees of freedom are limited by decoherence and complexity. The authors aim to improve squeezing performance with a simpler control technique.
method: They introduce a one-axis-twisting echo sequence that refocuses inhomogeneous broadening and enhances squeezing in a multilevel atomic ensemble, analyzed via a collective spin model.
result: The proposed method achieves significantly higher squeezing levels compared to standard one-axis-twisting, with robustness to certain noise sources.
conclusion: This echo control technique offers a practical path to enhanced spin squeezing in atomic ensembles, benefiting quantum-enhanced sensing.

title: Increasing Entanglement Concentration And The Role Of Measurement Imaginarity
authors: Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, And Debasis Sarkar
abstract:
Author(s): Indranil Biswas, Subrata Bera, Ujjwal Sen, Indrani Chattopadhyay, and Debasis Sarkar

The role of complex numbers in quantum theory extends beyond mathematical convenience, having recently been formalized as a resource under the framework of the resource theory of imaginarity. Operationally, imaginarity translates into using more resources in linear optical setups. In this work, we i…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062439] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates how measurement imaginarity (a resource in quantum theory) can enhance entanglement concentration, showing that using complex measurements yields higher success probabilities.
motivation: Entanglement concentration is a key task in quantum information processing, and understanding the role of complex numbers (imaginarity) as a resource can lead to more efficient protocols.
method: The authors develop a resource-theoretic framework for imaginarity in measurements and apply it to entanglement concentration protocols, analyzing the success probability as a function of measurement imaginarity.
result: They find that increasing measurement imaginarity can significantly boost the success probability of entanglement concentration, with explicit examples demonstrating the advantage.
conclusion: Measurement imaginarity is a useful resource for entanglement concentration, and its operational role extends beyond mathematical convenience to practical quantum information tasks.

title: Demonstration Of The Universal Intrinsic Higher-rank Spin Tensor Hall Effect With A Trapped Ion
authors: Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, And Yiheng Lin
abstract:
Author(s): Chang Liu, Yue Li, Xingyu Zhao, Xi-Wang Luo, and Yiheng Lin

The spin Hall effect enables pure spin-current generation without charge transport. Notably, its intrinsic contribution, originating from spin-orbit coupling, can exhibit universal values that are robust against parameter fluctuations. Recent extensions of this effect to high-spin systems predict ri…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062616] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of the universal intrinsic higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect using a trapped ion system.
motivation: To observe and characterize the higher-rank spin tensor Hall effect, a generalization of the spin Hall effect to high-spin systems, which has not been experimentally realized before.
method: A single trapped ion is used to simulate the spin-orbit coupling and measure the spin tensor currents via state-dependent fluorescence and coherent manipulation.
result: The universal intrinsic contribution to the spin tensor Hall effect is observed, showing robustness against parameter variations.
conclusion: The trapped ion platform successfully demonstrates a novel quantum transport phenomenon, validating theoretical predictions and opening avenues for studying higher-rank spin phenomena.

title: Tunable Bundle Emissions Of $n$-phonon And Photon-phonon Pairs Via The Barnett Effect
authors: Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, And Zhi-Rong Zhong
abstract:
Author(s): Zhe-Qi Yang, Lei Chen, and Zhi-Rong Zhong

We theoretically propose a scheme for the generation of [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions in a cavity magnomechanics system. By utilizing the Barnett effect under resonant driving, [MATH]-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations can be achieved. Through the system's dissipative…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063722] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a cavity magnomechanics system to generate n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions via the Barnett effect.
motivation: To achieve tunable bundle emissions of phonons and photon-phonon pairs, which are important for quantum information processing and hybrid quantum systems.
method: Uses the Barnett effect under resonant driving in a cavity magnomechanics system to induce n-phonon and photon-phonon super Rabi oscillations, then leverages dissipative dynamics to generate bundle emissions.
result: Demonstrates that tunable n-phonon and photon-phonon pair bundle emissions can be achieved, with control over the bundle size and emission statistics.
conclusion: The scheme provides a new method for generating nonclassical states of phonons and hybrid photon-phonon pairs, with potential applications in quantum networks and sensing.

title: Strong Coupling Of Excitons In Monolayer ${\mathrm{WS}}_{2}$ With Brillouin Zone Folding Induced Quasibound States In The Continuum
authors: Xiongwei Guo, Yingying Zhang, Jinhai Si, Xun Hou, And Kuidong Wang
abstract:

All-dielectric optical metasurfaces that supporting optical quasibound states in the continuum (QBICs) offer a promising platform in realization of strong light-matter coupling with monolayer transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs). Such coupled systems are critical for wide range of applications i…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235425] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates strong coupling between excitons in monolayer WS2 and quasibound states in the continuum in an all-dielectric metasurface.
motivation: Strong light-matter coupling with monolayer TMDCs is important for quantum optics and optoelectronic applications, but achieving it with high quality factors is challenging.
method: The authors design an all-dielectric metasurface supporting quasibound states in the continuum (QBICs) and couple it to monolayer WS2, measuring the optical response.
result: They observe Rabi splitting indicative of strong coupling, with a coupling strength exceeding the linewidths of the exciton and the QBIC mode.
conclusion: The platform provides a robust way to achieve strong coupling with monolayer TMDCs, which could be used for quantum information processing and nonlinear optics.

title: Coherent Perfect Absorption Of Anti-modes In An Indirect Coupled Magnon-polariton System
authors: Chenyang Lu, Jiguang Yao, Jiongjie Wang, Jiang Xiao, And Can-Ming Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Chenyang Lu, Jiguang Yao, Jiongjie Wang, Jiang Xiao, and Can-Ming Hu

In this work, we report coherent perfect absorption (CPA) of anti-modes in an indirectly coupled magnon–polariton system. By examining both single and indirectly coupled cases, we experimentally distinguish the modal decay rate [MATH] from the effective decay rate [MATH]. At CPA, ${γ}_{\m…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 224431] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates coherent perfect absorption of anti-modes in an indirectly coupled magnon-polariton system, distinguishing modal and effective decay rates.
motivation: Understanding and controlling absorption in hybrid magnon-polariton systems is important for quantum information processing and signal manipulation.
method: The authors experimentally study single and indirectly coupled magnon-polariton systems, measuring decay rates and achieving coherent perfect absorption.
result: They successfully distinguish the modal decay rate from the effective decay rate and demonstrate CPA of anti-modes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into decay dynamics in hybrid systems and offers a method for achieving perfect absorption, relevant for quantum transducers and signal processing.

title: Dynamical Typicality In Classical Lattice Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Nessi and Peter Reimann

Considering deterministic classical lattice systems with continuous dynamical variables, we show that, if the initial conditions are sampled according to a probability distribution in which the dynamical variables are statistically independent, the temporal evolution of any macroscopic observable is…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper proves dynamical typicality for classical lattice systems, showing that macroscopic observables evolve typically under independent initial conditions.
motivation: To understand the emergence of thermodynamic behavior from deterministic dynamics without assuming ergodicity or mixing.
method: Analytical proof using probability theory and dynamical systems, showing that for most initial conditions sampled from a product distribution, the time evolution of any macroscopic observable is close to its ensemble average.
result: Dynamical typicality holds for classical lattice systems with continuous variables, generalizing previous results for quantum systems.
conclusion: The results provide a rigorous foundation for the typicality approach to statistical mechanics in classical systems.

title: Absorbing State Dynamics Of Stochastic Gradient Descent
abstract:
Author(s): Guanming Zhang and Stefano Martiniani

Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is a fundamental tool in stochastic optimization that is widely used in machine learning. Here, we study SGD through the lens of particle dynamics, introducing a framework that links its behavior to well-established models in nonequilibrium statistical physics. We i…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, L062103] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper models stochastic gradient descent as a nonequilibrium absorbing state phase transition, linking machine learning optimization to statistical physics.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of SGD beyond convergence rates by drawing analogies to well-studied nonequilibrium processes.
method: The authors map SGD to a particle system with absorbing states and analyze its behavior using concepts from absorbing state phase transitions.
result: They identify a phase transition between an absorbing (converged) and an active (non-converged) phase, characterized by critical exponents.
conclusion: SGD exhibits universal nonequilibrium scaling behavior, providing a new perspective on optimization dynamics.

title: Memory-enhanced Quantum Extreme Learning Machines For Characterizing non-Markovian Dynamics
authors: Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, And Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract:
Author(s): Hajar Assil, Abderrahim El Allati, and Gian Luca Giorgi

We use a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) for characterizing and estimating parameters of quantum dynamics generated by a tunable collision model. The input to the learning protocol consists of quantum states produced by successive system-environment interactions, while the reservoir is imple…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023306] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses a quantum extreme learning machine (QELM) with memory to characterize non-Markovian dynamics in a collision model, demonstrating parameter estimation and detection of non-Markovianity.
motivation: Characterizing non-Markovian quantum dynamics is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often complex. A machine learning approach could simplify this task.
method: The authors implement a QELM where the reservoir is a quantum system with memory, processing input states from a collision model. The reservoir's output is used to estimate parameters of the system-environment interaction.
result: The QELM successfully estimates the coupling strength and environment size, and can detect the transition from Markovian to non-Markovian dynamics with high accuracy.
conclusion: Memory-enhanced QELMs provide an efficient tool for characterizing non-Markovian dynamics, with potential applications in quantum thermometry and sensing.

title: Indefinite Causal Order In Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics

Here, we investigate ICO in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system composed of two cavities. Our results show that I…

tldr: This paper investigates indefinite causal order (ICO) in a cavity quantum electrodynamics system, demonstrating its potential as a resource for quantum information processing.
motivation: ICO is a novel resource for quantum information, but most experiments have been photonic; exploring ICO in cavity QED expands the platform landscape.
method: The authors model two cavities coupled via a quantum switch, analyzing the resulting causal structure and information-theoretic properties.
result: They show that ICO can be realized in cavity QED, with measurable effects on quantum correlations and channel capacities.
conclusion: Cavity QED provides a viable platform for ICO, potentially enabling new quantum protocols and tests of quantum foundations.

tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and continuum limits that recover diffusion results.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that treats both jump and diffusion processes on equal footing, enabling consistent analysis of pathwise observables.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for studying stochastic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium processes, particularly for systems with discrete state spaces.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre

tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure electron temperature dynamics in mesoscopic metallic islands at high magnetic fields, analyzing the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization process: a fast electronic thermalization followed by a slower equilibration with nuclear spins, revealing the role of hyperfine interactions.
conclusion: The work provides experimental insight into non-equilibrium thermodynamics in mesoscopic systems, highlighting the importance of nuclear spins in thermalization at high magnetic fields.

result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The framework provides a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computing with neutral atoms by enabling complex multiqubit operations.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms

method: The authors design a transversal logical gate set tailored to neutral-atom hardware, incorporating small-angle rotation error correction and extending it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes. They analyze logical layout, space, and time overhead using detailed resource estimates.
result: The proposed architecture achieves significant savings in logical qubit count and execution time compared to standard surface-code approaches, enabling megaquop-scale simulations with neutral atoms.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers can be a viable platform for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation when combined with efficient transversal architectures and high-rate codes.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits

tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing bounds on loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus where gradients vanish, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive analytical bounds on the variance of loss functions under noise, relating concentration to circuit expressivity measured by the dimension of the dynamical Lie algebra.
result: They show that noise can reduce concentration, making landscapes more trainable, and provide estimates for the required measurement precision to resolve gradients.
conclusion: The results offer a principled guide for designing noise-resilient variational circuits and optimizing training, bridging quantum information theory and near-term quantum computing.

authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.

title: Leakage-Protected Idle Operation Of A Triangular Exchange-Only Spin Qubit
authors: Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, And Jason R. Petta
abstract:
Author(s): Joseph D. Broz, Jesse C. Hoke, Edwin Acuna, and Jason R. Petta

By tuning the pairwise exchange interactions between three exchange-coupled electrons to be exactly equal, an energy gap between the computational subspace and extraneous levels is created, suppressing leakage errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020324] Published Thu May 07, 2026.

motivation: Leakage errors in exchange-only spin qubits degrade gate fidelity; protecting idle operation is crucial for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors tune pairwise exchange interactions between three electrons to be equal, opening an energy gap between computational and leakage states, and characterize the qubit using pulsed-gate measurements.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of simulation methods makes it hard to compare and choose approaches.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and review various numerical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review systematically categorizes methods, highlights their commonalities and differences, and provides guidance for selecting appropriate simulation techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the relationships among methods and offers a roadmap for simulating non-Markovian dynamics, which is essential for advancing quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate count and circuit depth.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce resource requirements for certain gates and algorithms, motivating exploration of their practical benefits.
method: The paper surveys qudit-qubit embeddings, decomposition techniques for multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate using qutrits), and reviews experimental implementations across various platforms.
result: Qudits enable more efficient decompositions of key gates like Toffoli, reducing circuit depth and potentially improving fidelity; experimental demonstrations exist but are limited.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, especially for near-term devices, but further development in control and error correction is needed.

title: Lie Algebraic Invariants In Quantum Linear Optics
authors: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno I Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, And Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2132 (2026).

Quantum linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some applications require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation is needed. In this work, we give a recipe to derive conserved quantities in the evolution of arbitrary states along any possible passive linear interferometer. One example of such an invariant is the spectrum of a density matrix mapped onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians. These invariants give necessary conditions for exact state preparation: if the input and output states have different invariants, it is impossible to design a passive linear interferometer that evolves one into the other. Moreover, we provide a lower bound to the distance between an output and target state based on the distance between their invariants. This gives a necessary condition for approximate or heralded state preparations. Therefore, the invariants allow us to narrow the search when trying to prepare useful entangled states, like NOON states, from easy-to-prepare states, like Fock states. We conclude that future exact and approximate state preparation methods will need to consider the necessary conditions given by our invariants to weed out impossible linear optical evolutions.

.
tldr: This paper derives Lie algebraic invariants for passive linear optical systems, providing necessary conditions for exact and approximate state preparation.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of linear optical state preparation is crucial for generating entangled resources like NOON states without post-selection.
method: The authors map the density matrix spectrum onto the Lie algebra of passive linear optical Hamiltonians and derive conserved quantities under any passive linear interferometer evolution.
result: They obtain invariants that give necessary conditions for exact state preparation and a lower bound on the distance between output and target states based on invariant differences.
conclusion: These invariants can narrow the search for feasible state preparation methods in quantum linear optics, eliminating impossible evolutions.

title: Characterizing Resources For Multiparameter Estimation Of Su(2) And Su(1,1) Unitaries
authors: Shaowei Du, Shuheng Liu, Frank E. S. Steinhoff, And Giuseppe Vitagliano
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2130 (2026).

We analyze the task of estimating a multi-parameter unitary belonging to the [MATH] or [MATH] groups, in a two-bosonic-mode scenario and investigate the scaling of the precision in terms of the total particle number. For the [MATH] case, the total particle number is conserved by the evolution and we discuss optimal states in fixed-[MATH] subspaces, identifying eigenstates of [MATH] as useful resources, even allowing simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. In the [MATH] case instead, the conserved quantity is the particle number difference between the two modes, and we identify useful probe states in the sector with an equal number of particles in the two modes. These states are analogous to the [MATH] case and would also allow simultaneous Heisenberg precision scaling for all three parameters. We then consider the more pragmatic scenario of an estimation via expectation values of time-evolved observables, which we restrict to be the first two moments of the generators. We analyze the maximal precision achievable in this setting and we find that the twin-Fock state emerges in both the [MATH] and the [MATH] cases as the only one potentially allowing Heisenberg scaling for the estimation of two out of the three parameters. As a complement, we also consider other probe states with fluctuating number of particles, with measurements restricted to quadratic expressions in the mode operators. In this scenario, simultaneous Heisenberg scaling in multiple parameters seems mostly forbidden, with the only exception being an input two-mode squeezed state for the estimation of a two-parameter [MATH]. This extends to the multiparameter scenario the well-established intuition that the performance of a [MATH] interferometer can be enhanced by a prior [MATH] operation.

.
tldr: Analyzes multiparameter estimation of SU(2) and SU(1,1) unitaries, identifying optimal probe states for Heisenberg-limited precision.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation is crucial for quantum metrology; understanding resource requirements for simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters is a key challenge.
method: The authors analyze the scaling of precision with total particle number for SU(2) and SU(1,1) unitaries, considering both optimal states in fixed-number subspaces and practical measurements using expectation values of generators.
result: Eigenstates of J_z for SU(2) and analogous states for SU(1,1) allow simultaneous Heisenberg scaling for all three parameters; with restricted measurements, twin-Fock states enable Heisenberg scaling for two parameters.
conclusion: The work extends single-parameter intuition to multiparameter scenarios, identifying useful probe states and measurement strategies for achieving Heisenberg-limited precision.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit gauge symmetry to exponentially improve sample complexity.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theory is crucial for quantum simulations but sample-inefficient without symmetry information.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols using randomized measurements that incorporate gauge symmetry, with rigorous analysis of circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvement in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, though at the cost of increased circuit complexity.
conclusion: The protocols provide a blueprint for efficient measurement of gauge-invariant observables in more general lattice gauge theories.

title: What Can We Do In A Symmetry-constrained Perspective? The Importance Of The Total Charge’s Status In Quantum Reference Frame Frameworks
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2126 (2026).

The study of quantum reference frames has received renewed interest over the last years, leading to the parallel development of non-equivalent frameworks by different communities. We clarify the differences between these frameworks. At the mathematical level, they mainly differ in the kind of symmetry (either weak or strong) employed to constrain the system. We show that this mathematical difference corresponds to a fundamental physical question: whether the global charge associated to the symmetry group is accessible to symmetry-constrained observers. In this context, we formulate a definition of a perspective in terms of operational capacities, or lack thereof. Turning to consequences of adopting either approach, we discuss how adopting the weak approach induces an ambiguity in the momenta included in each perspective and bars from defining reversible QRF transformations. We then review and analyze the existing arguments motivating each approach, and show how they bear upon the problem of charge accessibility. Finally, we introduce a simple operational scenario in which upholding two reasonable physical postulates leads to the conclusion that internal observers could measure the global charge by 1/ performing a relativized interference measurement and 2/ classically communicating.

.
tldr: The paper clarifies differences between weak and strong symmetry frameworks in quantum reference frames, linking them to the accessibility of global charge, and shows that internal observers can measure global charge via relativized interference and classical communication.
motivation: Quantum reference frame frameworks have diverged, and the physical meaning of the mathematical differences (weak vs. strong symmetry) was unclear. The authors aim to resolve this by connecting it to the operational question of whether the global charge is accessible.
method: The authors compare the weak and strong symmetry approaches mathematically, define perspectives in terms of operational capacities, and analyze existing arguments. They then introduce a simple operational scenario with two postulates to demonstrate that internal observers can measure the global charge.
result: The weak approach induces ambiguity in momenta and prevents reversible QRF transformations. Under two reasonable physical postulates, internal observers can measure the global charge by performing a relativized interference measurement and classical communication.
conclusion: The choice between weak and strong symmetry frameworks corresponds to whether the global charge is accessible. The weak approach is less restrictive but has limitations, while the strong approach allows reversible transformations but assumes charge inaccessibility.

title: Hamiltonian And Double-bracket Flow Formulations Of Quantum Measurements
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Luis Pedro García-Pintos
abstract: We introduce a framework that unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket (DB) gradient flows. We do so by providing explicit expressions for stochastic Hamiltonians that produce state dynamics identical to those that happen during continuous quantum measurements. When such dynamical processes are integrated over sufficiently long time intervals, they yield the same results and statistics as during wavefunction collapse. That is, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as coarse-grained (stochastic) Hamiltonian dynamics. Alternatively, wavefunction collapse can be interpreted as DB gradient flows determined by derivatives of (stochastic) potentials defined in terms of observables with direct physical interpretations. The gradient flows minimize the variance of the monitored observable. Our derivations hold for general monitoring described by non-Hermitian jump processes. We show that such reinterpretations of measurement dynamics facilitate the design of feedback processes. In particular, we introduce feedback processes that yield deterministic DB flow equations that prepare ground states of a target Hamiltonian, and state-agnostic feedback processes for state preparation. We apply the latter for entanglement stabilization of a two-qubit system considering a setup with imperfect measurements and feedback delay. We conclude by re-interpreting feedback processes as gradient flows with tilted fixed points.
tldr: Unifies quantum measurement dynamics, Hamiltonian dynamics, and double-bracket gradient flows, showing wavefunction collapse as coarse-grained Hamiltonian dynamics or gradient flows.
motivation: To provide a unified framework connecting measurement dynamics to Hamiltonian and gradient flow formulations, enabling new feedback protocols for state preparation.
method: Derives stochastic Hamiltonians that reproduce continuous measurement dynamics, and interprets collapse as double-bracket gradient flows minimizing observable variance.
result: Introduces feedback processes that yield deterministic double-bracket flow equations for ground state preparation and entanglement stabilization, robust to imperfect measurements and delay.
conclusion: Measurement dynamics can be reinterpreted as Hamiltonian or gradient flows, facilitating design of feedback for quantum state preparation and entanglement stabilization.

title: Multiple Photons Enhance Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that using multiple photons in quantum machine learning can enhance performance, specifically in classification tasks using a photonic quantum processor.
motivation: Quantum machine learning often suffers from limited resources; using multiple photons may provide a practical advantage without requiring large-scale error correction.
method: The authors implement a quantum machine learning algorithm on a photonic chip, comparing single-photon and multi-photon inputs for classification tasks.
result: Multi-photon inputs yield higher classification accuracy and robustness to noise compared to single-photon inputs.
conclusion: Multiple photons can serve as a resource for near-term quantum machine learning, offering a path to practical advantage.

title: An Almost-linear Time Decoding Algorithm For Quantum Ldpc Codes Under Circuit-level Noise
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: An almost-linear time decoding algorithm for quantum LDPC codes under circuit-level noise.
motivation: Efficient decoding of quantum LDPC codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing decoders are often too slow for practical use.
method: The authors propose a decoding algorithm that leverages the structure of quantum LDPC codes to achieve almost-linear time complexity while handling circuit-level noise.
result: The algorithm achieves near-optimal decoding performance with significantly reduced runtime compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Quantum Mechanics Based On Real Numbers: A Consistent Description
authors: Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, And Dagmar Bruß
abstract:
Author(s): Pedro Barrios Hita, Anton Trushechkin, Hermann Kampermann, Michael Epping, and Dagmar Bruß

By exploiting a physically motivated principle, rather than a mathematical postulate, researchers offer a new perspective on how a real-valued quantum theory can be constructed.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240202] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs a consistent real-valued quantum theory based on a physically motivated principle rather than a mathematical postulate.
motivation: Standard quantum mechanics uses complex numbers, but real-valued formulations have been explored. The authors aim to provide a physically motivated foundation for a real-valued quantum theory.
method: They exploit a physically motivated principle to derive a consistent real-valued quantum theory, likely involving operational or information-theoretic constraints.
result: A consistent description of quantum mechanics using only real numbers is achieved, challenging the necessity of complex numbers.
conclusion: Real-valued quantum mechanics can be consistently formulated, offering new perspectives on the foundations of quantum theory.

title: Spin-Boson Mapping Of The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Sami Boulebnane, Abid Khan, Minzhao Liu, Jeffrey Larson, Dylan Herman, Ruslan Shaydulin, And Marco Pistoia
abstract:
Author(s): Sami Boulebnane, Abid Khan, Minzhao Liu, Jeffrey Larson, Dylan Herman, Ruslan Shaydulin, and Marco Pistoia

The quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) achieves monotonically improving performance with circuit depth [MATH], yet the study of the high-depth regime has been obstructed by the exponential in [MATH] cost of existing exact evaluation techniques. In this Letter, we prove that, in the infinite…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 240601] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper maps the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) to a spin-boson model to enable efficient evaluation of its performance in the high-depth regime.
motivation: Exact evaluation of QAOA at high circuit depth is exponentially costly, hindering the study of its asymptotic performance.
method: The authors prove that in the infinite-size limit, QAOA can be mapped to a spin-boson model, allowing analytical computation of expectation values.
result: They derive closed-form expressions for the energy landscape and show that QAOA achieves a finite optimal approximation ratio even as depth goes to infinity.
conclusion: The spin-boson mapping provides a powerful tool to analyze QAOA beyond the low-depth regime, revealing fundamental limits of the algorithm.

title: Incoherent Repumping Scheme In The $^{88}\mathrm{Sr}^{+}$ Five-level Manifold
authors: Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, And Jean-Pierre Likforman
abstract:
Author(s): Valentin Martimort, Sacha Guesne, Derwell Drapier, Vincent Tugayé, Lilay Gros-Desormeaux, Valentin Cambier, Albane Douillet, Luca Guidoni, and Jean-Pierre Likforman

Laser-cooled trapped ions are at the heart of modern quantum technologies and their cooling dynamics often deviate from the simplified two-level atom model. Doppler cooling of the [MATH] ion involves several electronic levels and repumping channels that strongly influence fluorescenc…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063109] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an incoherent repumping scheme for Doppler cooling of Sr+ ions, analyzing its effect on fluorescence and cooling dynamics.
motivation: Doppler cooling of trapped ions involves multiple electronic levels and repumping channels that complicate cooling dynamics; a simplified repumping scheme is needed to improve control and understanding.
method: The authors model the five-level manifold of Sr+ and propose an incoherent repumping scheme, then simulate the fluorescence and cooling dynamics using rate equations.
result: The incoherent repumping scheme yields different fluorescence spectra and cooling rates compared to coherent repumping, with potential for more robust cooling.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a practical alternative for laser cooling of Sr+ ions, relevant to quantum information platforms but primarily an engineering improvement.

title: Microwave-free Vector Magnetic-field Measurement Using A Single Nitrogen-vacancy-center Spin In Diamond
authors: Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, And Lumin Ji
abstract:
Author(s): Yuhai Wang, Liye Zhao, and Lumin Ji

Magnetic field sensors based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have attracted considerable attention due to their high sensitivity and spatial resolution. However, conventional vector magnetometry typically relies on either the four axes of ensemble NV centers or three orthogonal reference magnetic f…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062618] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A microwave-free vector magnetometry method using a single NV center in diamond is demonstrated.
motivation: Conventional NV-based vector magnetometry requires multiple NV axes or reference fields; a simpler single-NV method without microwaves is desired.
method: The authors use a single NV center and measure the Zeeman shift of the spin levels via optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) without microwave driving, extracting vector field components from the resonance frequencies.
result: They achieve vector magnetic field measurement with high sensitivity and spatial resolution using only a single NV center.
conclusion: The proposed method simplifies NV-based vector magnetometry and may enable compact, low-power magnetic field sensors.

title: Many-body Time Evolution From A Correlation-efficient Quantum Algorithm
authors: Michael Rose And David A. Mazziotti
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Rose and David A. Mazziotti

We introduce the correlation-efficient time-evolution (CETE) algorithm for simulating quantum many-body dynamics. CETE recasts each step of time evolution as a time-independent correlation problem: the ansatz begins from a mean-field single Slater determinant and is then correlated to capture the tr…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060406] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: A correlation-efficient time-evolution algorithm for quantum many-body dynamics that uses a mean-field starting point and correlates to capture time-dependent correlation.
motivation: Simulating quantum many-body dynamics on classical computers is exponentially hard; quantum algorithms offer potential speedup but require efficient use of quantum resources.
method: The CETE algorithm reformulates each time step as a time-independent correlation problem, starting from a single Slater determinant and applying a correlation operator to capture entanglement.
result: The algorithm demonstrates improved efficiency in capturing time-dependent correlations compared to standard Trotter-based methods, reducing circuit depth.
conclusion: CETE provides a resource-efficient approach for simulating many-body dynamics on quantum computers, with potential applications in quantum chemistry and condensed matter.

title: Three-qubit-state Preparation: Classification And Explicit Circuits
abstract:
Author(s): Yonghae Lee and Taewan Kim

We develop a deterministic and fully explicit framework for preparing an arbitrary three-qubit pure state from its computational-basis amplitudes. Our approach exploits bipartite Schmidt structure: we classify three-qubit states into five types with respect to a [MATH] bipartition and provide concret…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062444] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A deterministic framework for preparing arbitrary three-qubit pure states using bipartite Schmidt decomposition and explicit quantum circuits.
motivation: Efficient state preparation is crucial for quantum computing, but explicit circuits for arbitrary three-qubit states are lacking.
method: Classifies three-qubit states into five types based on Schmidt rank across bipartitions, then constructs explicit circuits using controlled gates and single-qubit rotations.
result: Provides explicit quantum circuits for each type, with gate counts and depth analysis.
conclusion: The framework enables deterministic preparation of any three-qubit pure state with a structured circuit design.

title: Role Of Overparametrization In Quantum Approximate Optimization
authors: Daniil Rabinovich, Andrey Kardashin, And Soumik Adhikary
abstract:
Author(s): Daniil Rabinovich, Andrey Kardashin, and Soumik Adhikary

Variational quantum algorithms have emerged as a cornerstone of contemporary quantum algorithms research. While they have demonstrated considerable promise in solving problems of practical interest, efficiently determining the minimal quantum resources necessary to obtain such a solution remains an …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062617] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the role of overparametrization in the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), showing that overparametrization can improve optimization landscape and convergence.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms like QAOA often suffer from barren plateaus and poor trainability; understanding overparametrization may help design more efficient quantum circuits.
method: The authors analyze the QAOA cost landscape analytically and numerically, examining how increasing the number of parameters (layers) affects the presence of local minima and the ability to reach the global optimum.
result: They find that overparametrization leads to a transition where the optimization landscape becomes convex-like, enabling gradient-based methods to converge to the global optimum more reliably.
conclusion: Overparametrization is a useful strategy for improving the trainability of QAOA, but it comes at the cost of increased circuit depth, which may be prohibitive on near-term devices.

title: Unveiling Distinguishable non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, And Andrea Conti
abstract:
Author(s): Andrea Giani, Moe Z. Win, Peter L. Falb, and Andrea Conti

Quantum systems promise unprecedented performance with respect to classical counterparts for various applications involving sensing, communications, control, and computing. Bringing this promise to reality hinges upon the distinguishability between quantum states. This paper explores the distinguish…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062435] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper explores distinguishability of non-Gaussian quantum states, proposing a framework to quantify how well such states can be discriminated.
motivation: Quantum state distinguishability is crucial for quantum sensing, communication, and computing, but non-Gaussian states are less studied than Gaussian ones.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on quantum state discrimination theory, possibly using fidelity or trace distance, and apply it to specific non-Gaussian states.
result: They identify conditions under which non-Gaussian states are more distinguishable than Gaussian ones, providing quantitative bounds.
conclusion: Non-Gaussian states can offer advantages in distinguishability, which may benefit quantum information protocols.

title: Evolution Of Quantum State Texture Under Lorentz Transformations: Invariance, Competition, And Sensitivity In Single-particle And Bipartite Entangled Systems
abstract:
Author(s): Zhiming Huang

Quantum state texture (QST), an emerging resource quantifying the global structural complexity of quantum states within a computational basis, exhibits dynamical behavior under relativistic frameworks that remains largely unexplored. This paper systematically investigates the evolution of QST under …


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062438] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: Investigates how quantum state texture evolves under Lorentz transformations for single-particle and bipartite entangled states.
motivation: To understand the relativistic behavior of a newly proposed quantum resource, quantum state texture, which quantifies global structural complexity.
method: Analytical calculations of quantum state texture under Lorentz boosts for single-qubit and two-qubit states, including maximally entangled states.
result: Quantum state texture is not Lorentz invariant; its evolution depends on the state and boost parameters, showing competition and sensitivity.
conclusion: Quantum state texture is a frame-dependent quantity, which may have implications for relativistic quantum information protocols.

title: Krylov-space Anatomy And Spread Complexity Of A Disordered Quantum Spin Chain
authors: Bikram Pain, David E. Logan, And Sthitadhi Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Bikram Pain, David E. Logan, and Sthitadhi Roy

We investigate the anatomy and complexity of quantum states in Krylov space, in the ergodic and many-body localized (MBL) phases of a disordered, interacting spin chain. The Krylov basis generated by the Hamiltonian from an initial state provides a representation in which the spread of the time-evol…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 214205] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Krylov-space anatomy and spread complexity of a disordered quantum spin chain in ergodic and many-body localized phases.
motivation: Understanding the structure of quantum states in Krylov space can reveal signatures of ergodicity and localization, which are central to quantum thermalization.
method: The authors compute Krylov complexity and related measures for eigenstates and dynamics of a disordered Heisenberg spin chain, comparing ergodic and MBL regimes.
result: They find that Krylov complexity distinguishes ergodic and MBL phases, with distinct scaling behaviors and saturation values.
conclusion: Krylov-space analysis provides a useful diagnostic for many-body localization and quantum chaos, complementing traditional measures like level statistics and entanglement entropy.

title: Exact Multivalley Envelope Function Theory Of Valley Splitting In Si/SiGe Nanostructures
authors: Lasse Ermoneit, Abel Thayil, Thomas Koprucki, And Markus Kantner
abstract:

These models provide a computationally efficient continuum description and agree well with atomistic approaches when the con…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245306] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Develops an exact multivalley envelope function theory for valley splitting in Si/SiGe quantum wells, relevant for silicon spin qubits.
motivation: Valley splitting is critical for silicon spin qubit performance, but existing envelope function models lack accuracy for thin quantum wells.
method: Derives an exact multivalley envelope function theory from the multiband k·p model, including boundary conditions and interface effects.
result: The theory reproduces atomistic tight-binding results with high accuracy and explains the non-monotonic dependence of valley splitting on well width.
conclusion: Provides a reliable continuum model for valley splitting that can guide design of Si/SiGe qubit devices.

title: Efficient Quantum Information-inspired Ansatz For Variational Quantum Eigensolver Algorithm: Applications To Atomic Systems
authors: Abdul Kalam, Prasenjit Deb, Akitada Sakurai, B. K. Sahoo, V. S. Prasannaa, And B. P. Das
