Chiral topological superconductors (TSCs) are conventionally characterized by the bulk Chern number, which dictates the number of chiral Majorana modes at the boundary. However, this single invariant often obscures the rich momentum-space structure of the superconducting gap. In this work, we unveil…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235426] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a skyrmion-resolved topological invariant to characterize chiral topological superconductors, revealing hidden momentum-space structure beyond the bulk Chern number.
motivation: The bulk Chern number alone obscures the rich momentum-space structure of the superconducting gap in chiral topological superconductors.
method: The authors define a skyrmion-resolved topological invariant based on the momentum-space skyrmion texture of the superconducting order parameter.
result: They show that the skyrmion-resolved invariant provides a finer classification of topological phases and predicts distinct Majorana edge mode signatures.
conclusion: The skyrmion-resolved topology offers a more detailed understanding of chiral topological superconductors and may guide experimental detection of topological phases.

title: Anomalous Floquet Higher-order Topological Superconducting Phases Induced By Unconventional Pairing Symmetries
authors: Donghao Wang, Yongchun Tao, Jingguo Hu, And Fengliang Huang
abstract:
Author(s): Donghao Wang, Yongchun Tao, Jingguo Hu, and Fengliang Huang

[Phys. Rev. B 113, 235427] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies higher-order topological superconductivity in Floquet-driven heterostructures with unconventional pairing symmetries.
motivation: To explore how periodic driving and unconventional pairing symmetries can induce anomalous Floquet higher-order topological superconducting phases.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling and numerical simulations of a ferromagnet–2D electron gas–superconductor heterostructure under periodic driving, analyzing topological invariants and edge states.
result: They find that unconventional pairing symmetries (d-wave, p+ip, etc.) lead to novel Floquet higher-order topological phases with Majorana corner modes.
conclusion: The work extends the understanding of Floquet topological phases to higher-order superconductivity, but is primarily a condensed matter physics result without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Large Isolated Stripes On Short 18-leg $t\text{−}J$ Cylinders
authors: Tizian Blatz, Sebastian Paeckel, Ulrich Schollwöck, Fabian Grusdt, And Annabelle Bohrdt
abstract:
Author(s): Tizian Blatz, Sebastian Paeckel, Ulrich Schollwöck, Fabian Grusdt, and Annabelle Bohrdt

Spin-charge stripes are among the most prominent competing orders in high-temperature superconductors. However, this phase is particularly challenging to study numerically due to finite-size effects. Here, we study the formation of long isolated stripes in the [MATH] model using…


[Phys. Rev. B 113, 245138] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper numerically studies spin-charge stripes in the t-J model on 18-leg cylinders, focusing on finite-size effects and stripe formation.
motivation: Spin-charge stripes are a competing order in high-temperature superconductors, but numerical studies are challenging due to finite-size effects.
method: Density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) simulations on long 18-leg t-J cylinders.
result: Observation of large isolated stripes and characterization of their properties.
conclusion: The study provides insights into stripe formation and finite-size effects in the t-J model.

conclusion: Altermagnets provide an efficient route to realize non-Hermitian higher-order topological phases.

method: Systematic investigation of topological transport properties and magnetostriction in heavy-element substituted Co-based all-d Heusler alloys, likely using first-principles calculations and experimental measurements.

title: Intercalation-induced Near Room-temperature Ferromagnetism In ${\mathrm{CrI}}_{3}$ Via Synergistic Exchange Pathways

motivation: To overcome the low Curie temperature of CrI3 for spintronic applications.

result: Intercalation leads to near room-temperature ferromagnetism through synergistic exchange pathways.
conclusion: Intercalation is a promising strategy to achieve room-temperature magnetic semiconductors.

result: They provide a full classification of SOTs and show how they drive spin dynamics in antiferromagnets.
conclusion: The work advances understanding of SOTs in antiferromagnets, which could enable efficient electrical control of antiferromagnetic devices.

authors: Ariel Nonato And Pedro D. S. Silva

In this work, we investigate the bi-isotropic effects in the formation and tunability of hybrid surface polaritons in bilayer configurations. result: Bi-isotropy introduces new hybrid polariton modes and allows tuning of their properties via external parameters.
conclusion: Bi-isotropic effects provide additional control over surface polaritons, which may be useful for nanophotonic applications.

tldr: This paper studies non-Hermitian quasiperiodic systems and discovers a new class of critical states called quasiperiodic skin criticality.
motivation: To understand how non-Hermiticity affects the nature of critical states in quasiperiodic systems, which are neither extended nor localized.

result: They find that non-Hermiticity gives rise to quasiperiodic skin criticality, where all eigenstates are critical and exhibit skin effect.

result: The model accurately reproduces a broad range of spectral, response, and thermodynamic properties observed in experiments.
conclusion: The interplay of correlations, strain, and relaxation is key to understanding twisted bilayer graphene's behavior.

conclusion: The absence of elastic anomalies suggests that quantum oscillations in insulators may not arise from conventional Fermi surface effects, pointing to an exotic electronic state.

title: Discontinuous Wealth-gradient Transition Driving Cooperation
authors: Hyun Gyu Lee, Hyeong-Chai Jeong, And Deok-Sun Lee

abstract:

tldr: This paper studies the scaling of fastest first-passage times in anomalous diffusion processes, focusing on subdiffusion and superdiffusion.
motivation: Many biophysical processes depend on the fastest searcher among many; understanding how the extreme first-passage time scales with the number of searchers is important for modeling such processes.
method: The author derives asymptotic formulas for the fastest first-passage time in various anomalous diffusion models, including subdiffusion and superdiffusion, using extreme value theory and stochastic analysis.

motivation: Understanding how long-range correlations affect eigenvalue distributions in non-Hermitian random matrices, which is a fundamental question in random matrix theory.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of the radial eigenvalue density for real random matrices with power-law decaying correlations.
result: A progressive breakdown of the circular law is observed as the correlation exponent decreases, with the radial density decaying faster than the circular law prediction.
conclusion: Long-range correlations significantly alter the spectral properties of non-Hermitian random matrices, leading to new universality classes.

title: Yielding In Dense Active Matter
authors: Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, And M. Lisa Manning
abstract:
Author(s): Adil Ghaznavi, Saverio Rossi, Francesco Zamponi, and M. Lisa Manning

High-density granular active matter is a useful model for dense animal collectives and could be useful for designing reconfigurable materials that can flow or solidify on command. Recent work has demonstrated key similarities and differences between the mechanical response of dense active matter and…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065410] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies yielding and mechanical response in dense granular active matter, a model for animal collectives and reconfigurable materials.
motivation: Understanding how dense active matter yields under stress is important for designing materials that can switch between solid and fluid states, and for modeling biological collectives.
method: The authors use numerical simulations of a dense granular active matter model, analyzing stress-strain curves and microscopic dynamics during yielding.
result: They identify key similarities and differences between active and passive yielding, including the role of activity in modifying the yield stress and strain.
conclusion: Activity can tune the mechanical response of dense granular materials, offering a route to control solid-fluid transitions.

title: Formation Of Bosonic $^{23}\mathrm{Na}^{41}\mathrm{K}$ Feshbach Molecules
authors: Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, And Jee Woo Park
abstract:
Author(s): Sungjun Lee, Younghoon Lim, Jongyeol Kim, Jaeryeong Chang, and Jee Woo Park

Ultracold Feshbach molecules are a crucial intermediate step for the creation of quantum degenerate gases of strongly dipolar molecules. After coherent transfer to the rovibrational ground state, these dimers can realize stable dipolar gases with strong, tunable long-range interactions. Here, we rep…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023307] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the formation of ultracold 23Na41K Feshbach molecules, a step toward creating quantum degenerate dipolar gases.
motivation: Ultracold Feshbach molecules are essential intermediates for producing strongly dipolar quantum gases with long-range interactions.
method: The authors use magnetoassociation across a Feshbach resonance in a mixture of 23Na and 41K atoms to form weakly bound molecules.
result: They successfully create Feshbach molecules and characterize their properties, including the Feshbach resonance location and molecule lifetime.
conclusion: This work provides a pathway to produce ultracold dipolar NaK molecules for studying strongly interacting quantum systems.

title: Most Probable Path And Invariant Sets In Noise-induced Transition To Turbulence
authors: Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, And Kenta Ishimoto
abstract:
Author(s): Yoshiki Hiruta, Kento Yasuda, and Kenta Ishimoto

Turbulence transition often arises from a subcritical transition between bistable states characterized by invariant sets of deterministic dynamical systems, and such transitions can be triggered by system noise as rare events. In this study, we employ the Onsager-Machlup (OM) formulation of stochast…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023303] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies noise-induced transitions to turbulence using the Onsager-Machlup formulation to find most probable paths and invariant sets.
motivation: Understanding turbulence transition from bistable states triggered by noise is important for predicting and controlling turbulent flows.
method: The authors apply the Onsager-Machlup functional to a stochastic dynamical system to compute most probable transition paths and identify invariant sets.
result: They characterize the most probable paths and invariant sets associated with the subcritical transition to turbulence.
conclusion: The work provides insight into noise-induced transitions in fluid turbulence, but does not connect to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Dynamical Phase Transitions Across Slow And Fast Regimes In A Two-tone Driven Duffing Resonator
authors: Soumya S. Kumar, Javier Del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, And Oded Zilberberg
abstract:
Author(s): Soumya S. Kumar, Javier del Pino, Letizia Catalini, Alexander Eichler, and Oded Zilberberg

The dynamical phase transitions of a Duffing resonator subjected to a bichromatic drive across the slow- and fast-beating regimes are mapped. An analytical threshold to observe these transitions based on an effective nonlinear response theory is provided, explaining the mechanism behind these processes. Complementary analytical treatments for the slow and fast regimes are supplied.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023298] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies dynamical phase transitions in a driven Duffing resonator, focusing on classical nonlinear dynamics rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the transition between slow and fast beating regimes in a nonlinear resonator under bichromatic drive.
method: Analytical effective nonlinear response theory combined with complementary treatments for slow and fast regimes.
result: An analytical threshold for dynamical phase transitions is derived and mapped across the two regimes.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for predicting and explaining dynamical phase transitions in driven nonlinear resonators.

title: Complete Inelastic Transparency Of Time-modulated Resonant Photonic Circuits
abstract:
Author(s): M. Sumetsky

Photonic circuits modulated in time can convert the input light frequency [MATH], shifting it by multiples of the modulation frequency [MATH] and, in certain cases, amplify the total input light power. Of special interest are photonic circuits employing microwave capacitors, which instantaneou…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023299] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies inelastic transparency in time-modulated resonant photonic circuits, focusing on frequency conversion and power amplification.
motivation: To understand how time modulation can achieve complete inelastic transparency, enabling efficient frequency conversion and amplification in photonic circuits.
method: Theoretical analysis using coupled-mode theory and Floquet formalism for time-periodic photonic structures.
result: Complete inelastic transparency is achieved when the modulation frequency matches the resonant frequency splitting, leading to perfect conversion of input light to a sideband with amplification.
conclusion: Time-modulated resonant photonic circuits can act as efficient frequency converters and amplifiers, with potential applications in classical and quantum photonics.

title: General Spin Models From Noncollinear Spin Density Functional Theory And Spin-cluster Expansion
abstract:
Author(s): Tomonori Tanaka and Yoshihiro Gohda

We present a data-efficient framework for constructing general classical spin Hamiltonians by combining the spin-cluster expansion (SCE) with fully self-consistent noncollinear spin density functional theory (DFT). The key idea is to fit the SCE model to magnetic torques rather than to total energie…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023300] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A data-efficient framework combining spin-cluster expansion with noncollinear spin DFT to construct classical spin Hamiltonians from magnetic torques.
motivation: To enable efficient and accurate construction of spin Hamiltonians for complex magnetic systems without relying on total energy calculations.
method: Uses spin-cluster expansion fitted to magnetic torques computed from self-consistent noncollinear spin DFT.
result: Demonstrates that fitting to torques yields accurate spin models with fewer DFT calculations compared to energy-based fitting.
conclusion: The torque-based SCE approach is a practical and efficient method for deriving spin Hamiltonians from first principles.

title: Current-induced Successive Structural Phase Transitions Beyond Thermal Equilibrium In Single-crystal ${\mathrm{VO}}_{2}$
authors: Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-Hisa Arima, And Ichiro Terasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shunsuke Kitou, Akitoshi Nakano, Masato Imaizumi, Yuiga Nakamura, Yuto Nakamura, Hideo Kishida, Taka-hisa Arima, and Ichiro Terasaki

Using synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy, current-induced structural phase transitions in single-crystal vanadium dioxide are investigated. Successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases are observed, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion inaccessible under thermal equilibrium.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022050] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports current-induced structural phase transitions in VO2, revealing a nonequilibrium metallic phase not accessible under thermal equilibrium.
motivation: To understand how electric current can drive structural phase transitions beyond thermal equilibrium, potentially enabling new phases and functionalities.
method: Synchrotron x-ray diffraction, optical microscopy, and Raman spectroscopy were used to characterize structural changes in single-crystal VO2 under applied current.
result: Successive transitions to two distinct metallic tetragonal phases were observed, including a nonequilibrium structure with isotropic lattice expansion.
conclusion: Current can induce structural phase transitions that are inaccessible by heating alone, demonstrating a pathway to novel nonequilibrium phases.

title: Visualizing Phonon Edge States On Molybdenum Disulfide
authors: Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, And Jakob Schiøtz
abstract:
Author(s): Patrick Giese, Mathias Stokkebye Nissen, Stig Helveg, and Jakob Schiøtz

Enhanced atomic vibrations have previously been observed near edges of two-dimensional materials with high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM). Here this observation is accounted for by localized phonon edge modes by including correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022049] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses HR-TEM image simulations to show that enhanced atomic vibrations near edges of MoS2 are due to localized phonon edge modes.
motivation: Enhanced atomic vibrations observed near edges of 2D materials in HR-TEM were not well understood; the authors aimed to explain this phenomenon.
method: They included correlated atom vibrations in HR-TEM image simulations to model the effect of phonon edge modes.
result: The simulations reproduced the enhanced vibrations, confirming that localized phonon edge modes are responsible.
conclusion: Phonon edge modes account for the observed enhanced atomic vibrations at edges of MoS2, providing insight into edge effects in 2D materials.

title: Emergent Self-attention From Astrocyte-gated Associative Memory Dynamics
abstract:
Author(s): Arnau Vivet and Alex Arenas

We introduce a Hopfield-type associative memory in which effective connectivity is multiplicatively modulated by astrocytic gains evolving under an entropy-regularized replicator equation. The coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics admit a Lyapunov function, ensuring global convergence. At fixed points, …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023276] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A Hopfield-type associative memory model with astrocyte-gated multiplicative modulation and entropy-regularized replicator dynamics, showing global convergence via a Lyapunov function.
motivation: To incorporate astrocytic modulation into neural network models of associative memory, bridging neuroscience and machine learning.
method: Introduces coupled neuron-astrocyte dynamics with a Lyapunov function and entropy-regularized replicator equation for astrocytic gains.
result: The model converges to fixed points where the effective connectivity matrix becomes a scaled identity, enabling emergent self-attention.
conclusion: The work provides a biologically plausible mechanism for self-attention in associative memory, but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tensor Network Approach To Momentum-resolved Spectroscopy In Nonperiodic Super-moiré Systems
authors: Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, And Jose L. Lado
abstract:
Author(s): Anouar Moustaj, Yitao Sun, Tiago V. C. Antão, and Jose L. Lado

Computing spectral functions in large, nonperiodic super-moiré systems remains an open problem due to the exceptionally large system size that must be considered. Here, we establish a tensor network methodology that allows computing momentum-resolved spectral functions of noninteracting and interact…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023282] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A tensor network method for computing momentum-resolved spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems.
motivation: Computing spectral functions in large nonperiodic super-moiré systems is challenging due to the huge system sizes required.
method: The authors develop a tensor network approach that efficiently computes momentum-resolved spectral functions for noninteracting and interacting systems.
result: The method enables spectral function calculations in systems with millions of atoms, demonstrated on twisted trilayer graphene and other moiré systems.
conclusion: The tensor network methodology provides a scalable tool for studying electronic properties of complex moiré systems.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains shows they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, detectable via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the quantum dynamics of chiral solitons in spin chains, which are topological excitations with potential relevance to low-dimensional magnetism.
method: Develops a nonperturbative quantization approach for chiral solitons and analyzes their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and their signature can be observed via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral soliton dynamics and predicts experimental observables.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop a non-perturbative method for studying strongly coupled conformal field theories using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to regularize fermionic CFTs and perform numerical simulations.
result: They find evidence of emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFTs on the fuzzy sphere.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study fermionic CFTs and can reveal emergent symmetries like supersymmetry.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures, demonstrating three distinct magnetic phases in EuAg4Sb2 and establishing a framework for spin-based vortex lattices.
motivation: Spin moiré superstructures offer a platform for manipulating information via spin textures, but a general theoretical framework for their design and characterization is lacking.
method: The authors combine neutron scattering, magnetization measurements, and theoretical modeling to map the magnetic phase diagram of EuAg4Sb2, revealing three tunable magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct magnetic phases are identified, and a design framework for spin-based vortex lattices is established.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures, with potential applications in information storage and manipulation.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: Theoretical study of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature.
motivation: To understand the stability of topological magnon gaps near the Curie point for spintronic applications.
method: Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures.
result: Topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point.
conclusion: Provides a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: Understanding causal relationships in complex networks is crucial but challenging; the authors aim to develop a general method using physical principles.
method: They propose a framework that leverages physical laws and network structure to predict causal links from observational data.
result: The framework successfully infers causal links across various networked dynamical systems, demonstrating broad applicability.
conclusion: The physics-informed approach provides a powerful tool for causal inference in networks, with potential applications in many fields.

title: General Framework Enabling Polarity-Tunable Time-Reversal Symmetric Superconducting Diode Effects In Gate-Defined Homojunctions
authors: Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, And Mingliang Tian
abstract:
Author(s): Hongwei Zhang, Chunsheng Wang, Ran Wang, Senyang Pan, Hengning Wang, Jiaqiang Cai, Yonglai Liu, Zhe Qu, Xiangde Zhu, Wei Ning, Chuanying Xi, Jinglei Zhang, Ning Hao, Guolin Zheng, and Mingliang Tian

Local protonic gating in
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021046] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a time-reversal symmetric superconducting diode effect in gate-defined homojunctions using local protonic gating.
motivation: To achieve magnetic-field-free control of nonreciprocal critical currents in superconducting diodes, which is important for low-dissipation electronics.
method: The authors use local protonic gating in homojunctions to induce a superconducting diode effect without breaking time-reversal symmetry.
result: They observe a polarity-tunable superconducting diode effect, enabling control of nonreciprocal critical currents without an external magnetic field.
conclusion: The work provides a general framework for realizing superconducting diodes in gate-defined homojunctions, with potential applications in superconducting electronics.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper predicts anyonic exciton superfluidity in quantum Hall bilayers at topological criticality.
motivation: To explore exotic collective quantum states in fractional quantum Hall systems beyond the conventional paradigm.
method: Theoretical analysis using topological field theory and mean-field approaches for quantum Hall bilayers.
result: Topological criticality enables anyonic exciton condensation, leading to a superfluid phase with anyonic statistics.
conclusion: Anyon superfluidity provides a robust mechanism for engineering novel quantum states in bilayer quantum Hall systems.

title: Three-Dimensional Xy Universality And Nonlinear Magnetic Susceptibility In A Kagome Ice Compound
authors: Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, And Philipp Gegenwart
abstract:
Author(s): Kan Zhao, Hao Deng, Hua Chen, Nvsen Ma, Noah Oefele, Jiesen Guo, Xueling Cui, Chen Tang, Matthias J. Gutmann, Thomas Mueller, Yixi Su, Vladimir Hutanu, Changqing Jin, and Philipp Gegenwart

Nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in the kagome spin ice HoAgGe reveal hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground states, reached via a three-dimensional XY universality class transition.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021043] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements in a kagome spin ice compound, revealing a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking.
motivation: To understand the nature of the ground state and phase transition in the kagome ice compound HoAgGe, which exhibits spin ice behavior and potential hidden order.
method: The authors performed nonlinear magnetic susceptibility measurements on single crystals of HoAgGe, combined with neutron scattering and other techniques, to probe the critical behavior and symmetry breaking.
result: They observed a three-dimensional XY universality class transition and evidence of hidden time-reversal symmetry breaking in the ground state.
conclusion: The study establishes HoAgGe as a system with a three-dimensional XY transition and hidden order, contributing to the understanding of frustrated magnetism and spin ice materials.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the discovery of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using ARPES.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) was used to measure the electronic band structure of layered transition-metal oxyhalides.
result: Intrinsic flat bands were observed that remain stable at room temperature, with orbital selectivity.
conclusion: These materials provide a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states at accessible temperatures.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Magneto-optical spectroscopy, specifically attractive polaron spectroscopy, is used to study the electronic and magnetic properties of twisted bilayer WSe2 under applied electric and magnetic fields.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and demonstration of electric-field-induced transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: The work establishes twisted bilayer WSe2 as a platform for studying and controlling topological magnetic phases, with potential for future quantum devices.

title: Liquid-Gas Criticality Of Hyperuniform Fluids
authors: Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, And Qun-Li Lei
abstract:
Author(s): Shang Gao, Hao Shang, Hao Hu, Yu-Qiang Ma, and Qun-Li Lei

Where ordinary fluids show wild fluctuations and critical opalescence, hyperuniform fluids of spinning particles stay unusually calm yet highly susceptible at the liquid–vapor critical point.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021032] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the critical behavior of hyperuniform fluids, a topic in soft condensed matter physics with no direct connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Hyperuniform fluids exhibit suppressed density fluctuations at large scales, and their critical behavior at the liquid-gas transition is of fundamental interest in statistical mechanics.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis and possibly simulations to characterize the critical exponents and scaling of hyperuniform fluids near the liquid-vapor critical point.
result: They find that hyperuniform fluids show unusual calmness yet high susceptibility at the critical point, contrasting with ordinary fluids.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the criticality of hyperuniform systems, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, or quantum hardware.

title: Stealthy-Hyperuniform Wave Dynamics In Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals
authors: Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, And Mikael C. Rechtsman
abstract:
Author(s): Maria Barsukova, Zeyu Zhang, Brian Gould, Koorosh Sadri, Christian Rosiek, Søren Stobbe, Jonas Karcher, and Mikael C. Rechtsman

While disordered stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be largely transparent within a particular range of wavelengths, new experiments on large-scale silicon photonic crystals reveal unexpected residual scattering driven by radiative loss.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021028] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies wave dynamics in disordered stealthy hyperuniform photonic crystals, revealing unexpected residual scattering from radiative loss.
motivation: Stealthy hyperuniform materials are expected to be transparent in certain wavelength ranges, but experiments show residual scattering that needs explanation.
method: Large-scale experiments on silicon photonic crystals combined with theoretical analysis of radiative loss mechanisms.
result: Unexpected residual scattering is driven by radiative loss, contradicting the expectation of near-perfect transparency.
conclusion: The findings highlight limitations of stealthy hyperuniformity for photonic applications and suggest design modifications.

title: Ballistic Spin Valve In Graphene Realized Via Electron Optics
authors: Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, And Ivan J. Vera-Marun
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Burrow, Oktay Deveci, Rares Dragomir, Thomas Thomson, and Ivan J. Vera-Marun

Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene reveals gate-tunable ballistic spin transport, providing a mechanism for coherent spin control through spin-dependent electron optics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021029] Published Thu May 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a ballistic spin valve in graphene using transverse magnetic focusing and electron optics.
motivation: To achieve coherent spin control in graphene via gate-tunable ballistic spin transport.
method: Transverse magnetic focusing in encapsulated graphene to reveal spin-dependent electron optics.
result: Observation of gate-tunable ballistic spin transport enabling a spin valve effect.
conclusion: Graphene can serve as a platform for coherent spin control through electron optics.

title: Dipolar Nematic State In Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, And Shi Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Yuan-Jinsheng Liu, Tyler C. Sterling, and Shi Liu

A nematic ordering underpins the behavior of relaxor ferroelectrics.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021022] Published Wed Apr 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics, focusing on condensed matter physics without connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Relaxor ferroelectrics exhibit complex ordering; understanding the nematic state may clarify their behavior.
method: The authors likely use experimental or theoretical methods to characterize the dipolar nematic phase.
result: Identification and description of a dipolar nematic state in relaxor ferroelectrics.
conclusion: The nematic ordering is key to relaxor ferroelectric properties.

title: More Is Less In Unpercolated Active Solids
authors: Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, And Anton Souslov
abstract:
Author(s): Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, and Anton Souslov

By combining experiments with robotic metamaterials and theory, this work shows that increasing microscopic activity can counterintuitively cause a solid’s macroscale active response to vanish when active units are too sparse for the active forces to percolate through the structure.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021012] Published Mon Apr 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies active solids where increasing microscopic activity can suppress macroscopic response due to lack of percolation.
motivation: To understand how sparse active units affect the collective mechanical response of active solids.
method: Combines robotic metamaterial experiments with theoretical modeling to probe the percolation of active forces.
result: Increasing activity can reduce or eliminate the macroscopic active response when active units are too sparse to percolate.
conclusion: The phenomenon 'more is less' arises from the interplay between activity and percolation, relevant for designing active metamaterials.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: The paper proposes a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in topological data analysis, claiming exponential speedup.
motivation: Topological data analysis is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that leverages quantum linear algebra and sampling techniques to compute persistent homology.
result: They prove a provable exponential quantum speedup over classical algorithms for certain instances of the problem.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a new application area for quantum computing, potentially enabling practical quantum advantage in data analysis.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A high-level perspective piece proposing a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, focusing on scientific milestones rather than technical results.
motivation: To outline a roadmap for bridging the gap between theoretical quantum computing and practical applications.
method: Conceptual framework based on expert opinion and analysis of current quantum computing progress.
result: A five-stage framework detailing milestones for quantum utility.
conclusion: The framework provides a structured path for the quantum computing community to focus efforts on achieving real-world impact.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, serving as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, and its approximation is a candidate for quantum advantage.
method: The authors design an end-to-end quantum algorithm that includes state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They demonstrate the algorithm on small knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and scaling analysis for larger instances.
conclusion: The work provides a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and suggests that the Jones polynomial approximation may offer a quantum advantage.

title: Photon Catalysis For General Multimode Multi-Photon Quantum State Preparation
authors: Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, And Massimo Frigerio
abstract:
Author(s): Andrei Aralov, Émilie Gillet, Viet Nguyen, Andrea Cosentino, Mattia Walschaers, and Massimo Frigerio

Using a procedure based on symmetric tensor decomposition, every photonic state can be prepared with realistic experimental tools and a predictable number of steps.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020323] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: A method for preparing arbitrary photonic states using symmetric tensor decomposition and photon catalysis.
motivation: Efficient preparation of complex photonic states is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are often limited to specific states or require many resources.
method: The authors use symmetric tensor decomposition to design a photon catalysis procedure that can generate any multimode multi-photon state with a predictable number of steps.
result: They demonstrate that the method works for general states and provide a constructive protocol using realistic experimental tools.
conclusion: Photon catalysis offers a universal and efficient approach for photonic state preparation, potentially advancing quantum computing and communication.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge in 2D magnetism, which has revealed new phenomena and challenged established theories.
method: The paper is a review, synthesizing experimental and theoretical results on 2D van der Waals magnetic materials.
result: The review covers ferromagnets, antiferromagnets, topology, quantum dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons, spintronics, and multiferroics.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving, expanding theoretical understanding and opening new directions for applications.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from geometric frustration and interference effects.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, synthesizing findings from multiple studies.
result: Kagome metals exhibit a wealth of exotic states including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, unconventional superconductivity, and orbital antiferromagnetism.
conclusion: The kagome lattice provides a rich platform for exploring correlated electron physics and may lead to new quantum states.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation, with broad applications to physical systems.
motivation: Spin glasses are a classic model for disordered systems, and understanding their dynamics is important for many areas of physics.
method: The paper reviews experimental results, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin-glass dynamics.
result: It highlights the synergy between experiment, theory, and simulation, and outlines future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass dynamics remain a rich field with open questions, and continued interdisciplinary work is needed.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to neural network data.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a fundamental challenge in neuroscience.
method: The authors review recent progress in connecting maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to recordings from thousands of neurons.
result: These methods uncover reproducible collective behaviors in neural populations.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a powerful framework for analyzing neural network data, achieving predictive power comparable to other areas of physics.

title: The Ups And Downs Of Internal Conversion
authors: Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, And Salvy P. Russo
abstract:
Author(s): Anjay Manian, Zifei Chen, Hugh T. Sullivan, and Salvy P. Russo

This review examines the theoretical methods used to describe the photophysical process of internal conversion in quantum systems. These models explore all facets of the nonradiative mechanism, and the review presents an outlook on how they can be incorporated in studies relevant to applications, for example, in photonics and energy harvesting.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035003] Published Tue Sep 16, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical methods for internal conversion in quantum systems, focusing on nonradiative transitions and applications in photonics and energy harvesting.
motivation: Internal conversion is a key photophysical process affecting the efficiency of light-emitting devices and solar energy conversion, yet its theoretical description remains challenging.
method: The review surveys various theoretical models, including nonadiabatic dynamics, Fermi's golden rule, and mixed quantum-classical approaches, to describe internal conversion.
result: The paper summarizes the strengths and limitations of current methods and identifies open challenges in modeling internal conversion in complex systems.
conclusion: Improved theoretical methods are needed to accurately predict internal conversion rates, which will aid in designing better photonic and energy-harvesting materials.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review of quantum aspects of magnetic skyrmions, covering formation interactions and quantum features.
motivation: To survey quantum-mechanical properties of skyrmions, which are topological spin textures with potential applications in spintronics.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion quantum mechanics, including quantum tunneling and entanglement.
result: Summarizes current understanding of quantum effects in skyrmions, such as quantum depinning and skyrmion qubits.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmionics is an emerging field with potential for quantum information but remains largely exploratory.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of theoretical and experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the Standard Model, including their potential connection to dark matter and dark energy.
motivation: To understand possible new physics beyond the Standard Model, particularly spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons that could explain dark matter and dark energy.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for spin-dependent interactions and surveys experimental techniques used to search for them, such as precision measurements and symmetry tests.
result: The review summarizes current constraints on various exotic spin-dependent interactions and highlights the most promising experimental approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential implications for fundamental physics, but no definitive evidence has been found yet.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium reviewing synthetic quantum matter in fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions, with applications to condensed matter and gravity.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries that are difficult to realize naturally, enabling simulation of topological phenomena and gravitational models.
method: Reviews experimental implementations in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems, and theoretical frameworks for fractal, curved, and higher-dimensional lattices.
result: Summarizes progress in realizing synthetic geometries and their potential for simulating exotic physics.
conclusion: Synthetic quantum matter in nonstandard geometries is a rapidly advancing field with connections to condensed matter and high-energy physics.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of using massive quantum systems to probe gravity, including tests of quantum gravity-induced decoherence and entanglement.
motivation: To understand the interplay between quantum mechanics and gravity, which is poorly understood, by using massive quantum systems as probes.
method: Review of theoretical proposals and experimental efforts, including matter-wave interferometry and tests of gravity-mediated entanglement.
result: Summarizes current theoretical frameworks and experimental progress, highlighting that no definitive evidence of quantum gravity effects has been observed yet.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems offer a promising avenue to test quantum gravity, but further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Qubit Operations Using A Modular Optical System Engineered With PyOpticL: A code-to-CAD Optical Layout Tool
authors: Jacob Myers, Christopher Caron, Nishat Helaly, Zhenyu Wei, Justin Oh, Zack Gotobed, Kotaro Yabe, And Robert J. Niffenegger
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2135 (2026).

Complex optical design is hindered by conventional piecewise setup, which prevents modularization and therefore abstraction of subsystems at the circuit level. This limits multiple fields that require complex optics systems, including quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions, because their optical systems are not scalable. We present an open-source Python library for optical layout (PyOpticL) which uses beam-path simulation and dynamic beam-path routing for quick and easy optical layout by placing optical elements along the beam path without a priori specification, enabling adaptive, path-based layouts with automatic routing and connectivity. We use PyOpticL to create modular `drop-in' optical baseplates for common optical subsystems used in atomic and molecular optics (AMO) experiments including laser sources, frequency and intensity modulation, and locking to an atomic reference for stabilization. We demonstrate this minimal working example of a dynamic full laser system for strontium trapped ions by using it for laser cooling, qubit state detection, and over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates with 3D printed baseplates. This enables a new paradigm of design abstraction layers for engineering optical systems leveraging modular baseplates, as they can be used for any wavelength in the system and enables scaling up the underlying optical systems for quantum computers. This new open-source hardware and software code-to-CAD library seeks to foster open-source collaborative hardware and systems design across numerous fields of research including AMO physics and quantum computing with neutral atoms and trapped ions.

.
tldr: Presents an open-source Python library for optical layout and modular baseplates for AMO experiments, demonstrated with trapped-ion qubit operations.
motivation: Complex optical design in quantum computing with atoms and trapped ions is not scalable due to conventional piecewise setup; a modular, abstracted approach is needed.
method: Develops PyOpticL, a Python library using beam-path simulation and dynamic routing, and creates modular 'drop-in' optical baseplates for common subsystems; demonstrates with a full laser system for strontium trapped ions.
result: Achieves over 99% fidelity single-qubit gates using 3D-printed baseplates, enabling scalable optical systems for quantum computers.
conclusion: The code-to-CAD approach and modular baseplates enable a new paradigm for engineering optical systems, fostering open-source collaborative hardware design for AMO physics and quantum computing.

title: Experimental Exclusion Of A Generalized Károlyházy Gravity-induced Decoherence Model
authors: Nicola Bortolotti, Kristian Piscicchia, Alessio Porcelli, Matthias Laubenstein, Simone Manti, Antonino Marcianò, Federico Nola And Catalina Curceanu
abstract: We report new experimental constraints on the generalized version of the gravity-induced decoherence model originally proposed by Károlyházy. Using data collected by the VIP Collaboration at the INFN Gran Sasso National Laboratory with a high-purity germanium detector, we derive an improved lower bound on the spatial correlation length characterizing metric fluctuations in the model. We obtain a bound m (95% C.L.), which exceeds by more than an order of magnitude the previous experimental limit. When combined with the theoretical upper bound m derived from macroscopic localization requirements, our result excludes the generalized Károlyházy model. The same conclusion applies to an associated non-Markovian formulation of the continuous spontaneous localization model. Our findings significantly tighten experimental constraints on gravity-related decoherence scenarios and demonstrate the sensitivity of underground low-background experiments to foundational modifications of quantum mechanics.
tldr: Experimental exclusion of a gravity-induced decoherence model using underground detector data.
motivation: To test foundational modifications of quantum mechanics that predict gravity-induced decoherence, which could affect quantum coherence in large systems.
method: Used high-purity germanium detector data from the VIP Collaboration at Gran Sasso to constrain the spatial correlation length of metric fluctuations in the generalized Károlyházy model.
result: Obtained an improved lower bound on the correlation length, exceeding previous limits by an order of magnitude, and combined with theoretical upper bounds to exclude the model.
conclusion: The generalized Károlyházy model is experimentally excluded, tightening constraints on gravity-related decoherence scenarios.

title: Kovacs-like Memory Effect In Strain Stiffening Collagen Networks
authors: Maitri Mandal And Sayantan Majumdar Abhishek Ghadai
abstract: Materials driven far from equilibrium can encode memories of past deformations through long-lived structural reorganizations. Such memory effects-reflecting parameters such as deformation direction, magnitude, and duration have been widely explored in soft amorphous solids. Here, we report a Kovacs-like memory effect manifested as a non-monotonic stress relaxation in vitro biopolymer networks formed by type-I collagen, an essential component of the mammalian extracellular matrix. Using shear rheology combined with in-situ optical imaging, we find that this memory effect emerges exclusively in the nonlinear strain-stiffening regime, and persists over a much broader range of strain amplitudes than previously reported for other viscoelastic amorphous materials. Furthermore, we uncover a strong correlation between the memory response and the development of negative normal stresses and associated strain fields, highlighting the unique nonequilibrium mechanics underlying memory formation in biopolymer networks.
tldr: This paper reports a Kovacs-like memory effect in strain-stiffening collagen networks, a soft matter system far from equilibrium.
motivation: To understand memory formation in biopolymer networks, which are important in biological contexts but not directly related to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Shear rheology combined with in-situ optical imaging to observe stress relaxation and normal stresses in collagen networks.
result: A non-monotonic stress relaxation (Kovacs-like memory) is observed only in the nonlinear strain-stiffening regime, correlated with negative normal stresses.
conclusion: The memory effect in collagen networks arises from unique nonequilibrium mechanics, but the work is purely classical soft matter physics.

title: Anisotropic Fluorescence Signals Retarded Dipole-dipole Interactions In A Thermal Atomic Cloud
authors: Vyacheslav Shatokhin, Friedemann Landmesser, Mario Niebuhr, Frank Stienkemeier, Andreas Buchleitner And Lukas Bruder
abstract: We experimentally observe and theoretically explain anisotropic multiple quantum coherence signals in the fluorescence from dilute thermal potassium vapours, at room temperature and particle densities . We identify the retarded part of the geometrically fully resolved inter-atomic, resonant dipole-dipole interaction as the crucial ingredient to theoretically reproduce all qualitative features of the experimental spectra.
tldr: Experimental and theoretical study of anisotropic fluorescence signals from thermal atomic vapors due to retarded dipole-dipole interactions.
motivation: To understand the role of retarded dipole-dipole interactions in anisotropic multiple quantum coherence signals observed in fluorescence from thermal atomic clouds.
method: Experimental observation of fluorescence from dilute thermal potassium vapors combined with theoretical modeling incorporating geometrically resolved retarded dipole-dipole interactions.
result: The retarded part of the dipole-dipole interaction is essential to reproduce all qualitative features of the experimental spectra.
conclusion: Retarded dipole-dipole interactions are crucial for explaining anisotropic fluorescence signals in thermal atomic clouds.

title: Direct Visualization Of Field-driven Valence Band Modulation In Electrostatically Reconfigured Graphene Devices
authors: Umidakhon Rayimjonova, Chin-Yi Huang, Yi-Cheng Weng, Elin Cartwright, Fredrik O L Johansson, Noemi Vannucchi, Pavel Dudin, Avila Jose, Pei Ding, David Muradas-Belinchón, Henry Nameirakpam, Zhaojun Li, Andreas Lindblad And M Venkata Kamalakar
abstract: Graphene with ultrathin metal-oxide layers has emerged as a scalable platform for integrated electronic, spintronic, and neuromorphic devices. The in-plane electric fields in such devices are typically inferred indirectly from transport measurements, which do not provide microscopic details of the interface potential profile. Here, we use photoemission microscopy to uncover the precise electrostatic landscape of a complete device comprising diverse, heterogeneous ultrathin metal-oxide-covered graphene junctions. Using in operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution, we directly image the real potential profile across an entire graphene device, including regions covered by AlOx and TiOx nanometer-thick overlayers. Tracking the valence band edge under current bias and gate voltage enables quantitative analysis of internal field evolution via a spectroscopic screening factor, revealing an up to more than 50% suppression of the electric field in graphene covered with oxides, in agreement with transport measurements. This demonstrates local reconfiguration of electric fields in graphene for advanced two-dimensional (2D) device engineering and circuitry, while our operando circuit spectroscopy measurements provide a generic means to uncover intricate potential landscapes and carrier redistribution in 2D electronic and spintronic circuits.
tldr: This paper uses photoemission microscopy to directly visualize the electrostatic potential profile in graphene devices with oxide overlayers, revealing field suppression due to dielectric screening.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic potential landscape in graphene devices is crucial for optimizing electronic and spintronic performance, but indirect transport measurements lack spatial resolution.
method: The authors employ in operando x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy with submicron resolution to image the valence band edge across a graphene device under bias and gate voltage, extracting a spectroscopic screening factor.
result: They observe up to 50% suppression of the electric field in graphene regions covered by AlOx and TiOx, consistent with transport measurements, demonstrating local field reconfiguration.
conclusion: Operando circuit spectroscopy provides a generic method to uncover potential landscapes in 2D devices, enabling advanced engineering of graphene-based circuits.

title: Percolation With Coupled Lasers: Effect Of Non-linearities On The Phase Transition
authors: Simon Mahler, Nikita Stroev, Mahmoud Abu Rmilah, Asher Friesem And Nir Davidson
abstract: Controlled experimental studies of percolation are challenging due to difficulties in tuning site connectivity, isolating local interactions, and mitigating finite-size effects. In this work, we experimentally investigate percolation with a platform of coupled lasers, where connectivity, interaction strength, and system size can be controlled. Using a square array of lasers with astronomical number of possible cluster configurations, we show that the emergence of a percolating cluster corresponds to the onset of phase locking among the lasers. We also show that the percolation probability undergoes a second-order alike transition as a function of the site-occupation probability, with a threshold consistent with classical theoretical predictions. Surprisingly, we find that at low pump level, amplified mode competition (nonlinear regime) alters the effective behavior of the lasing sites and modify the nature of the percolation transition. The experimental results are interpreted by the means of a theoretical toy model with connectivity rules to the classical percolation.
tldr: This paper experimentally studies percolation using a coupled laser array, showing that percolation corresponds to phase locking and that nonlinearities alter the transition.
motivation: Controlled experimental studies of percolation are difficult; coupled lasers offer a tunable platform to investigate percolation phenomena.
method: A square array of coupled lasers with controllable connectivity and pump levels is used to observe percolation and phase locking, with a toy model to interpret results.
result: Percolation probability undergoes a second-order-like transition consistent with classical theory, but nonlinearities at low pump levels modify the transition.
conclusion: Coupled lasers provide a versatile platform for studying percolation, and nonlinear effects can change the nature of the phase transition.

title: Nonreciprocal Electrical Transport In Emerging Noncentrosymmetric Systems: From Hidden Symmetry To Functional Devices
authors: Shengyao Li, Zherui Yang, Xueyan Wang, Kian Ping Loh And X Renshaw Wang
abstract: Contrary to the reciprocal electrical transport constrained by the Onsager relations, nonreciprocal electrical transport arises in noncentrosymmetric systems where the resistance depends on the direction of current flow or external stimuli such as a magnetic field. Governed by symmetry-dependent charge dynamics, these responses appear as nonreciprocal charge transport (NCT) in the longitudinal direction and the nonlinear Hall effect (NLHE) in the transverse direction. Recent theoretical advances have expanded the range of mechanisms and material platforms capable of hosting nonreciprocal signals, revealing the role of hidden band-geometric properties. In parallel, experimental developments have exploited these effects for practical devices, offering promising alternatives to semiconductor-based rectifiers and wireless components, with advantages in broadband operation, ultrafast response, and high energy efficiency. In this review, we summarize electrical measurement techniques and characteristic transport signatures for identifying nonreciprocal phenomena and uncovering their underlying symmetry. We provide a comprehensive discussion of the fundamental mechanisms underlying NCT and NLHE, organized through representative material systems, and a subsequent examination of strategies for artificially inducing and enhancing nonreciprocity. Finally, we evaluate the technological perspectives of nonreciprocal electrical transport for electronic applications, along with key challenges and opportunities for scalable device implementation. By synthesizing current progress, this review aims to guide materials discovery and device innovation, and to inspire exploration of new symmetry settings and unconventional routes toward enhanced nonreciprocal functionalities.
tldr: A review of nonreciprocal electrical transport in noncentrosymmetric systems, focusing on symmetry-dependent charge dynamics and device applications.
motivation: To understand and exploit nonreciprocal transport phenomena for novel electronic devices beyond conventional semiconductors.
method: Summarizes theoretical mechanisms (band-geometric properties) and experimental techniques for measuring nonreciprocal charge transport and nonlinear Hall effect.
result: Identifies material platforms and strategies to induce/enhance nonreciprocity, with potential for broadband, ultrafast, energy-efficient rectifiers and wireless components.
conclusion: Nonreciprocal electrical transport offers promising device functionalities, but challenges remain in scalable implementation and materials discovery.

title: Crystallography-driven Molecularization Of A Two-dimensional Spin- 3 / ...
authors: Hari Borutta, Tobias Müller, Ronny Thomale, Harald O Jeschke And Yasir Iqbal
abstract: Large-spin two-dimensional magnets are generally expected to develop conventional long-range order once the dominant exchange scale becomes appreciable. The layered spin- maple-leaf compound Na Mn O defies this expectation: despite sizable antiferromagnetic interactions and no evident disorder, it exhibits no magnetic ordering and displays two well-separated thermodynamic crossover scales. We show that this behavior originates from a crystallography-driven molecularization of the magnetic degrees of freedom. The low-symmetry structure partitions the Mn sublattice into inequivalent exchange pathways, generating a pronounced hierarchy that nearly isolates antiferromagnetic hexagons. Magnetic correlations therefore develop in two stages: first within individual hexagons at a scale set by the dominant exchange, and only at much lower temperatures do frustrated inter-hexagon couplings attempt to establish coherence across the lattice. While isolated hexagons reproduce the two-step thermodynamic structure, the experimentally relevant temperature scales emerge only once the hexagons are embedded in the frustrated two-dimensional network. The resulting quantum ground state is magnetically disordered, characterized by strong intra-hexagon correlations and rapidly decaying inter-hexagon correlations. These results identify crystallographic inequivalence as a materials-level mechanism for stabilizing molecularized and quantum-disordered states even in large-spin two-dimensional magnets.
tldr: This paper explains the absence of magnetic order in a large-spin 2D magnet via crystallography-driven molecularization into weakly coupled antiferromagnetic hexagons.
motivation: To understand why the layered spin-3/2 compound NaMn2O4 does not magnetically order despite strong antiferromagnetic interactions and no disorder.
method: The authors perform electronic structure calculations and model the magnetic system using a Heisenberg Hamiltonian on the maple-leaf lattice, analyzing exchange hierarchies and thermodynamic properties.
